عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنِ الْأَسْوَدِ قَالَ: دَخَلَ شَبَابٌ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ عَلَى عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا وَهِيَ بِمِنًى وَهُمْ يَضْحَكُونَ. فَقَالَتْ: مَا يُضْحِكُكُمْ؟ قَالُوا: فُلَانٌ خَرَّ عَلَى طُنُبِ فُسْطَاطٍ فَكَادَتْ عُنُقُهُ أَوْ عَيْنُهُ أَنْ تَذْهَبَ. فَقَالَتْ: لَا تَضْحَكُوا. إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ (ﷺ) قَالَ: «مَا مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ يُشَاكُ شَوْكَةً فَمَا فَوْقَهَا إِلَّا كُتِبَتْ لَهُ بِهَا دَرَجَةٌ وَمُحِيَتْ بِهَا عَنْهُ خَطِيئَةٌ»[^2]. يَحْتَمِلُ: فَمَا عَدَا الشَّوْكَةَ وَتَجَاوَزَهَا فِي الْقِلَّةِ، وَهِيَ نَحْوُ نُخْبَةِ النَّمْلَةِ فِي قَوْلِهِ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ: «مَا أَصَابَ الْمُؤْمِنَ مِنْ مَكْرُوهٍ فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لِخَطَايَاهُ حَتَّى نُخْبَةُ النَّمْلَةِ»[^3]، وَهِيَ عَضَّتُهَا. وَيَحْتَمِلُ مَا هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنَ الشَّوْكَةِ وَأَوْجَعُ، كَالْخُرُورِ عَلَى طُنُبِ الْفُسْطَاطِ. فَإِنْ قُلْتَ: كَيْفَ يُضْرَبُ الْمَثَلُ بِمَا دُونَ الْبَعُوضَةِ وَهِيَ النِّهَايَةُ فِي الصِّغَرِ؟ قُلْتُ: لَيْسَ كَذَلِكَ، فَإِنَّ جَنَاحَ الْبَعُوضَةِ أَقَلُّ مِنْهَا وَأَصْغَرُ بِدَرَجَاتٍ، وَقَدْ ضَرَبَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) مَثَلًا لِلدُّنْيَا[^4]، وَفِي خَلْقِ اللَّهِ حَيَوَانٌ أَصْغَرُ مِنْهَا وَمِنْ جَنَاحِهَا، رُبَّمَا رَأَيْتَ فِي تَضَاعِيفِ الْكُتُبِ الْعَتِيقَةِ دُوَيْبَّةً لَا يَكَادُ يُجَلِّيهَا لِلْبَصَرِ الْحَادِّ إِلَّا تَحَرُّكُهَا، فَإِذَا سَكَنَتْ فَالسُّكُونُ يُوَارِيهَا، ثُمَّ إِذَا لَوَّحْتَ لَهَا بِيَدِكَ حَادَتْ عَنْهَا وَتَجَنَّبَتْ مَضَرَّتَهَا، فَسُبْحَانَ مَنْ يُدْرِكُ صُورَةَ تِلْكَ وَأَعْضَاءَهَا الظَّاهِرَةَ وَالْبَاطِنَةَ وَتَفَاصِيلَ خِلْقَتِهَا وَيُبْصِرُ بَصَرَهَا وَيَطَّلِعُ عَلَى ضَمِيرِهَا، وَلَعَلَّ فِي خَلْقِهِ مَا هُوَ أَصْغَرُ مِنْهَا وَأَصْغَرُ ﴿Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows and of themselves and of what they do not know﴾. وَأَنْشَدْتُ لِبَعْضِهِمْ:

يَا مَنْ يَرَى مَدَّ البَعُوضِ جَنَاحَهَا ... فِي ظُلْمَةِ اللَّيْلِ البَهِيمِ الأَلْيَلِ
وَيَرَى عُرُوقَ نِيَاطِهَا فِي نَحْرِهَا ... وَالمُخَّ فِي تِلْكَ العِظَامِ النَّحَّلِ
اغْفِرْ لِعَبْدٍ تَابَ مِنْ فَرَطَاتِهِ ... مَا كَانَ مِنْهُ فِي الزَّمَانِ الأَوَّلِ[^5]

وَ**فَأَمَّا** حَرْفٌ فِيهِ مَعْنَى الشَّرْطِ، وَلِذَلِكَ يُجَابُ بِالْفَاءِ. وَفَائِدَتُهُ فِي الْكَلَامِ أَنْ يُعْطِيَهُ فَضْلَ تَوْكِيدٍ. تَقُولُ: زَيْدٌ ذَاهِبٌ. فَإِذَا قَصَدْتَ تَوْكِيدَ ذَاكَ، وَأَنَّهُ لَا مَحَالَةَ ذَاهِبٌ، وَأَنَّهُ بِصَدَدِ الذَّهَابِ، وَأَنَّهُ مِنْهُ عَزِيمَةٌ، قُلْتَ: أَمَّا زَيْدٌ فَذَاهِبٌ. وَلِذَلِكَ قَالَ سِيبَوَيْهِ فِي تَفْسِيرِهِ: مَهْمَا يَكُنْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَزَيْدٌ ذَاهِبٌ. وَهَذَا التَّفْسِيرُ مُدِلٌّ لِفَائِدَتَيْنِ: بَيَانِ كَوْنِهِ تَوْكِيدًا، وَأَنَّهُ فِي مَعْنَى الشَّرْطِ. فَفِي إِيرَادِ الْجُمْلَتَيْنِ مُصَدَّرَتَيْنِ بِهِ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يُقَلْ: فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَعْلَمُونَ، وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يَقُولُونَ، إِحْمَادٌ عَظِيمٌ لِأَمْرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَاعْتِدَادٌ بِعِلْمِهِمْ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ، وَنَعْيٌ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ إِغْفَالَهُمْ حَظَّهُمْ وَعِنَادَهُمْ وَرَمْيَهُمْ بِالْكَلِمَةِ الْحَمْقَاءِ. وَ**الْحَقُّ** الثَّابِتُ الَّذِي لَا يَسُوغُ إِنْكَارُهُ. يُقَالُ: حَقَّ الْأَمْرُ، إِذَا ثَبَتَ وَوَجَبَ. ﴿وَحَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ﴾[^6]، وَثَوْبٌ مُحَقَّقٌ: مُحْكَمُ النَّسْجِ. وَ**مَاذَا** فِيهِ وَجْهَانِ: أَنْ يَكُونَ «ذَا» اسْمًا مَوْصُولًا بِمَعْنَى «الَّذِي»، فَيَكُونَ كَلِمَتَيْنِ. وَأَنْ يَكُونَ «ذَا» مُرَكَّبَةً مَعَ «مَا» مَجْعُولَتَيْنِ اسْمًا وَاحِدًا فَتَكُونَ كَلِمَةً وَاحِدَةً، فَهُوَ عَلَى الْوَجْهِ الْأَوَّلِ مَرْفُوعُ الْمَحَلِّ عَلَى الِابْتِدَاءِ وَخَبَرُهُ «ذَا» مَعَ صِلَتِهِ. وَعَلَى الثَّانِي مَنْصُوبُ الْمَحَلِّ فِي حُكْمِ «مَا» وَحْدَهُ لَوْ قُلْتَ: مَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ. وَالْأَصْوَبُ فِي جَوَابِهِ أَنْ يَجِيءَ عَلَى الْأَوَّلِ مَرْفُوعًا، وَعَلَى الثَّانِي مَنْصُوبًا، لِيُطَابِقَ الْجَوَابُ السُّؤَالَ. وَقَدْ جَوَّزُوا عَكْسَ ذَلِكَ، تَقُولُ فِي جَوَابِ مَنْ قَالَ: مَا رَأَيْتَ؟ خَيْرٌ، أَيِ الْمَرْئِيُّ خَيْرٌ. وَفِي جَوَابِ: مَاذَا الَّذِي رَأَيْتَ؟ خَيْرًا، أَيْ رَأَيْتُ خَيْرًا. وَقُرِئَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ قُلِ الْعَفْوَ﴾[^7] بِالرَّفْعِ وَالنَّصْبِ عَلَى التَّقْدِيرَيْنِ. وَ**الْإِرَادَةُ** نَقِيضُ الْكَرَاهَةِ، وَهِيَ مَصْدَرُ أَرَدْتُ الشَّيْءَ إِذَا طَلَبَتْهُ نَفْسُكَ وَمَالَ إِلَيْهِ قَلْبُكَ. وَفِي حُدُودِ الْمُتَكَلِّمِينَ: الْإِرَادَةُ مَعْنًى يُوجِبُ لِلْحَيِّ حَالًا لِأَجْلِهَا يَقَعُ مِنْهُ الْفِعْلُ عَلَى وَجْهٍ دُونَ وَجْهٍ. وَقَدِ اخْتَلَفُوا فِي إِرَادَةِ اللَّهِ، فَبَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى أَنَّ لِلْبَارِئِ مِثْلَ صِفَةِ الْمُرِيدِ مِنَّا الَّتِي هِيَ الْقَصْدُ، وَهُوَ أَمْرٌ زَائِدٌ عَلَى كَوْنِهِ عَالِمًا غَيْرَ سَاهٍ. وَبَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى أَنَّ مَعْنَى إِرَادَتِهِ لِأَفْعَالِهِ هُوَ أَنَّهُ فَعَلَهَا وَهُوَ غَيْرُ سَاهٍ وَلَا مُكْرَهٍ. وَمَعْنَى إِرَادَتِهِ لِأَفْعَالِ غَيْرِهِ أَنَّهُ أَمَرَ بِهَا. وَالضَّمِيرُ فِي ﴿أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ﴾ لِلْمَثَلِ، أَوْ لِأَنْ يُضْرَبَ. وَفِي قَوْلِهِمْ: ﴿مَاذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِهَذَا مَثَلًا﴾ اسْتِرْذَالٌ وَاسْتِحْقَارٌ، كَمَا قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا فِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِي[^8]: يَا عَجَبًا لِابْنِ عَمْرٍو هَذَا؟ «**مَثَلًا**» نُصِبَ عَلَى التَّمْيِيزِ، كَقَوْلِكَ لِمَنْ أَجَابَ بِجَوَابٍ غَثٍّ: مَاذَا أَرَدْتَ بِهَذَا جَوَابًا؟ وَلِمَنْ حَمَلَ سِلَاحًا رَدِيئًا: كَيْفَ تَنْتَفِعُ بِهَذَا سِلَاحًا؟ أَوْ عَلَى الْحَالِ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿هَذِهِ نَاقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً﴾[^9]. وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿يُضِلُّ بِهِ كَثِيرًا وَيَهْدِي بِهِ كَثِيرًا﴾ جَاءَ مَجْرَى التَّفْسِيرِ وَالْبَيَانِ لِلْجُمْلَتَيْنِ الْمُصَدَّرَتَيْنِ بِ«أَمَّا»، وَأَنَّ فَرِيقَ الْعَالِمِينَ بِأَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ وَفَرِيقَ الْجَاهِلِينَ الْمُسْتَهْزِئِينَ بِهِ كِلَاهُمَا مَوْصُوفٌ بِالْكَثْرَةِ، وَأَنَّ الْعِلْمَ بِكَوْنِهِ حَقًّا مِنْ بَابِ الْهُدَى الَّذِي ازْدَادَ بِهِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ نُورًا إِلَى نُورِهِمْ، وَأَنَّ الْجَهْلَ بِحُسْنِ مَوْرِدِهِ مِنْ بَابِ الضَّلَالَةِ الَّتِي زَادَتِ الْجَهَلَةَ خَبْطًا فِي ظُلْمَائِهِمْ. فَإِنْ قُلْتَ: لِمَ وُصِفَ الْمَهْدِيُّونَ بِالْكَثْرَةِ وَالْقِلَّةُ صِفَتُهُمْ[^10]؟ قُلْتُ: أَهْلُ الْهُدَى كَثِيرٌ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ، وَحِينَ يُوصَفُونَ بِالْقِلَّةِ إِنَّمَا يُوصَفُونَ بِهَا بِالْقِيَاسِ إِلَى أَهْلِ الضَّلَالِ. وَأَيْضًا فَإِنَّ الْقَلِيلَ مِنَ الْمَهْدِيِّينَ كَثِيرٌ فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ وَإِنْ قَلُّوا فِي الصُّورَةِ، فَسُمُّوا ذَهَابًا إِلَى الْحَقِيقَةِ كَثِيرًا:

إِنَّ الكِرَامَ كَثِيرٌ فِي البِلَادِ وَإِنْ ... قَلُّوا كَمَا غَيْرُهُمْ قَلَّ وَإِنْ كَثُرُوا[^11]

وَ﴿قَلِيلٌ مِنْ عِبَادِيَ الشَّكُورُ﴾[^12]، ﴿وَقَلِيلٌ مَا هُمْ﴾[^13]. النَّاسُ كَإِبِلٍ مِائَةٍ لَا تَجِدُ فِيهَا رَاحِلَةً. وَجَدْتَ النَّاسَ أَخْبَرَ تَقْلُهُ؟

وَإِسْنَادُ الْإِضْلَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى إِسْنَادُ الْفِعْلِ إِلَى السَّبَبِ[^14]: لِأَنَّهُ لَمَّا ضَرَبَ الْمَثَلَ فَضَلَّ بِهِ قَوْمٌ وَاهْتَدَى بِهِ قَوْمٌ، تَسَبَّبَ لِضَلَالِهِمْ وَهُدَاهُمْ. وَعَنْ مَالِكِ بْنِ دِينَارٍ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ دَخَلَ عَلَى مَحْبُوسٍ قَدْ أُخِذَ بِمَالٍ عَلَيْهِ وَقُيِّدَ، فَقَالَ: يَا أَبَا يَحْيَى، أَمَا تَرَى مَا نَحْنُ فِيهِ مِنَ الْقُيُودِ؟ فَرَفَعَ مَالِكٌ رَأْسَهُ فَرَأَى سَلَّةً. فَقَالَ: لِمَنْ هَذِهِ السَّلَّةُ؟ فَقَالَ: لِي، فَأَمَرَ بِهَا تُنْزَلُ، فَإِذَا دَجَاجٌ وَأَخْبِصَةٌ، فَقَالَ مَالِكٌ: هَذِهِ وَضَعَتِ الْقُيُودَ عَلَى رِجْلِكَ. وَقَرَأَ زَيْدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: ﴿يَضِلُّ بِهِ كَثِيرًا﴾[^15]. وَكَذَلِكَ: ﴿وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِ إِلَّا الْفَاسِقِينَ﴾[^16]. وَ**الْفِسْقُ**: الْخُرُوجُ عَنِ الْقَصْدِ. قَالَ رُؤْبَةُ:

فَوَاسِقًا عَنْ قَصْدِهَا جَوَائِرَا[^17]

وَ**الْفَاسِقُ** فِي الشَّرِيعَةِ: الْخَارِجُ عَنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ بِارْتِكَابِ الْكَبِيرَةِ، وَهُوَ النَّازِلُ بَيْنَ الْمَنْزِلَتَيْنِ[^18] أَيْ بَيْنَ مَنْزِلَةِ الْمُؤْمِنِ وَالْكَافِرِ، وَقَالُوا: إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَنْ حَدَّ لَهُ هَذَا الْحَدَّ: أَبُو حُذَيْفَةَ وَاصِلُ بْنُ عَطَاءٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ وَعَنْ أَشْيَاعِهِ[^19]. وَكَوْنُهُ بَيْنَ بَيْنَ أَنَّ حُكْمَهُ حُكْمُ الْمُؤْمِنِ فِي أَنَّهُ يُنَاكَحُ وَيُوَارَثُ وَيُغَسَّلُ وَيُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ وَيُدْفَنُ فِي مَقَابِرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ. وَهُوَ كَالْكَافِرِ فِي الذَّمِّ وَاللَّعْنِ وَالْبَرَاءَةِ مِنْهُ وَاعْتِقَادِ عَدَاوَتِهِ، وَأَنْ لَا تُقْبَلَ لَهُ شَهَادَةٌ. وَمَذْهَبُ مَالِكِ بْنِ أَنَسٍ وَالزَّيْدِيَّةِ[^20]: أَنَّ الصَّلَاةَ لَا تُجْزِئُ خَلْفَهُ. وَيُقَالُ لِلْخُلَفَاءِ الْمَرَدَةِ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ: الْفَسَقَةُ. وَقَدْ جَاءَ الِاسْتِعْمَالَانِ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: ﴿بِئْسَ الِاسْمُ الْفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ الْإِيمَانِ﴾[^21] يُرِيدُ اللَّمْزَ وَالتَّنَابُزَ، ﴿إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ﴾[^22].

**النَّقْضُ**: الْفَسْخُ وَفَكُّ التَّرْكِيبِ. فَإِنْ قُلْتَ: مِنْ أَيْنَ سَاغَ اسْتِعْمَالُ النَّقْضِ فِي إِبْطَالِ الْعَهْدِ؟ قُلْتُ: مِنْ حَيْثُ تَسْمِيَتُهُمُ الْعَهْدَ بِالْحَبْلِ عَلَى سَبِيلِ **الِاسْتِعَارَةِ**[^23]، لِمَا فِيهِ مِنْ ثَبَاتِ الْوُصْلَةِ بَيْنَ الْمُتَعَاهِدَيْنِ. وَمِنْهُ قَوْلُ ابْنِ التَّيِّهَانِ فِي بَيْعَةِ الْعَقَبَةِ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ حِبَالًا وَنَحْنُ قَاطِعُوهَا، فَنَخْشَى إِنْ أَعَزَّكَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَأَظْهَرَكَ أَنْ تَرْجِعَ إِلَى قَوْمِكَ»[^24]. وَهَذَا مِنْ أَسْرَارِ الْبَلَاغَةِ وَلَطَائِفِهَا أَنْ يَسْكُتُوا عَنْ ذِكْرِ الشَّيْءِ الْمُسْتَعَارِ، ثُمَّ يَرْمُزُوا إِلَيْهِ بِذِكْرِ شَيْءٍ مِنْ رَوَادِفِهِ، فَيُنَبِّهُوا بِتِلْكَ الرَّمْزَةِ عَلَى مَكَانِهِ. وَنَحْوُهُ قَوْلُكَ: شُجَاعٌ يَفْتَرِسُ أَقْرَانَهُ، وَعَالِمٌ يَغْتَرِفُ مِنْهُ النَّاسُ، وَإِذَا تَزَوَّجْتَ امْرَأَةً فَاسْتَوْثِرْهَا. لَمْ تَقُلْ هَذَا إِلَّا وَقَدْ نَبَّهْتَ عَلَى الشُّجَاعِ وَالْعَالِمِ بِأَنَّهُمَا أَسَدٌ وَبَحْرٌ، وَعَلَى الْمَرْأَةِ بِأَنَّهَا فِرَاشٌ[^25]. وَ**الْعَهْدُ**: الْمُوَثَّقُ. وَعَهِدَ إِلَيْهِ فِي كَذَا: إِذَا وَصَّاهُ بِهِ وَوَثَّقَهُ عَلَيْهِ. وَاسْتَعْهَدَ مِنْهُ: إِذَا اشْتَرَطَ عَلَيْهِ وَاسْتَوْثَقَ مِنْهُ. وَالْمُرَادُ بِهَؤُلَاءِ النَّاقِضِينَ لِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ: أَحْبَارُ الْيَهُودِ الْمُتَعَنِّتُونَ، أَوْ مُنَافِقُوهُمْ، أَوِ الْكُفَّارُ جَمِيعًا. فَإِنْ قُلْتَ: فَمَا الْمُرَادُ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ؟ قُلْتُ: مَا رُكِزَ فِي عُقُولِهِمْ مِنَ الْحُجَّةِ عَلَى التَّوْحِيدِ، كَأَنَّهُ أَمَرَ وَصَّاهُمْ بِهِ وَوَثَّقَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ، وَهُوَ مَعْنَى قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى﴾[^26]. أَوْ أَخْذُ الْمِيثَاقِ عَلَيْهِمْ بِأَنَّهُمْ إِذَا بُعِثَ إِلَيْهِمْ رَسُولٌ يُصَدِّقُهُ اللَّهُ بِمُعْجِزَاتِهِ صَدَّقُوهُ وَاتَّبَعُوهُ، وَلَمْ يَكْتُمُوا ذِكْرَهُ فِيمَا تَقَدَّمَهُ مِنَ الْكُتُبِ الْمُنَزَّلَةِ عَلَيْهِمْ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِي أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ﴾[^27]. وَقَوْلُهُ فِي الْإِنْجِيلِ لِعِيسَى صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ: «سَأُنَزِّلُ عَلَيْكَ كِتَابًا فِيهِ نَبَأُ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ، وَمَا أَرَيْتُهُ إِيَّاهُمْ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ، وَمَا أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَا نَقَضُوا مِنْ مِيثَاقِهِمُ الَّذِي وَاثَقُوا بِهِ، وَمَا ضَيَّعُوا مِنْ عَهْدِهِ إِلَيْهِمْ». وَحُسْنُ صُنْعِهِ لِلَّذِينَ قَامُوا بِمِيثَاقِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى وَأَوْفَوْا بِعَهْدِهِ، وَنَصْرُهُ إِيَّاهُمْ، وَكَيْفَ أَنْزَلَ بَأْسَهُ وَنِقْمَتَهُ بِالَّذِينَ غَدَرُوا وَنَقَضُوا مِيثَاقَهُمْ وَلَمْ يُوفُوا بِعَهْدِهِ، لِأَنَّ الْيَهُودَ فَعَلُوا بِاسْمِ عِيسَى مَا فَعَلُوا بِاسْمِ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمَا وَسَلَّمَ مِنَ التَّحْرِيفِ وَالْجُحُودِ وَكَفَرُوا بِهِ كَمَا كَفَرُوا بِمُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ. وَقِيلَ: هُوَ أَخْذُ اللَّهِ الْعَهْدَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَنْ لَا يَسْفِكُوا دِمَاءَهُمْ، وَلَا يَبْغِيَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ، وَلَا يَقْطَعُوا أَرْحَامَهُمْ. وَقِيلَ: عَهْدُ اللَّهِ إِلَى خَلْقِهِ ثَلَاثَةُ عُهُودٍ: الْعَهْدُ الْأَوَّلُ الَّذِي أَخَذَهُ عَلَى جَمِيعِ ذُرِّيَّةِ آدَمَ، الْإِقْرَارُ بِرُبُوبِيَّتِهِ[^28] وَهُوَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ﴾[^29]، وَعَهْدٌ خُصَّ بِهِ النَّبِيُّونَ أَنْ يُبَلِّغُوا الرِّسَالَةَ وَيُقِيمُوا الدِّينَ وَلَا يَتَفَرَّقُوا فِيهِ، وَهُوَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مِيثَاقَهُمْ﴾[^30]، وَعَهْدٌ خُصَّ بِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ وَهُوَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَكْتُمُونَهُ﴾[^31]. وَالضَّمِيرُ فِي «مِيثَاقِهِ» لِلْعَهْدِ، وَهُوَ مَا وَثَّقُوا بِهِ عَهْدَ اللَّهِ مِنْ قَبُولِهِ وَإِلْزَامِهِ أَنْفُسَهُمْ. وَيَجُوزُ أَنْ يَكُونَ بِمَعْنَى تَوْثِقَتِهِ، كَمَا أَنَّ الْمِيعَادَ وَالْمِيلَادَ بِمَعْنَى الْوَعْدِ وَالْوِلَادَةِ. وَيَجُوزُ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ الضَّمِيرُ إِلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى، أَيْ مِنْ بَعْدِ تَوْثِقَتِهِ عَلَيْهِمْ، أَوْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا وَثَّقَ بِهِ عَهْدَهُ مِنْ آيَاتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَإِنْذَارِ رُسُلِهِ. وَمَعْنَى قَطْعِهِمْ مَا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُوصَلَ: قَطْعُهُمُ الْأَرْحَامَ وَمُوَالَاةَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَقِيلَ قَطْعُهُمْ مَا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ مِنَ الْوُصْلَةِ وَالِاتِّحَادِ وَالِاجْتِمَاعِ عَلَى الْحَقِّ، فِي إِيمَانِهِمْ بِبَعْضٍ وَكُفْرِهِمْ بِبَعْضٍ. فَإِنْ قُلْتَ: مَا الْأَمْرُ؟ قُلْتُ:

---

الناس ألف منهم كواحد ... وواحد كألف إن أمر عرا
وأما الآية فمضمونها أن عدد المهديين كثير في نفسه، ومضمون الآيات الأخر أن عددهم قليل بالنسبة إلى كثرة عدد الضالين، فعُبِّر عنه تارة بالكثرة نظرًا إلى ذاته، وتارة بالقلة نظرًا إلى غيره، فليس معنى البيت من الآية في شيء.
[^11]: القَلّ، بالفتح: القليل، وهو المراد. وبالضم: بمعنى القلة، ويستعمل بمعنى القليل أيضًا. وبالكسر: الارتعاد غضبًا. يقول: إن الكرام في الدنيا كثير لكثرة خيرهم، لأن الكريم يقاوم ألف لئيم، والحال أنهم قليل في العدد كما أن غيرهم، يعني اللئام، قليل في الخير وإن كثروا في العدد. فوجه الشبه اجتماع الكثرة والقلة في كل على التوزيع.

Seeking an act from one who is beneath you and urging him to it. From this is named the matter (al-amr), which is the singular of "affairs" (al-umur), because the call which summons the one who undertakes it resembles a commander who orders him to do it; so it is said of it "amr," naming the object by the verbal noun, as if it were "ma'mur bihi" (that which is commanded). Likewise it is called "sha'n." The sha'n is the seeking and the intention. It is said: "sha'antu sha'nahu," meaning, I intended his intention.

﴿They are the losers﴾, because they exchanged breaking for fulfilment, severing for joining, and corruption for righteousness, and its punishment for its reward.

This verse was revealed to show that what the ignorant, the foolish, and the stubborn disputers among the disbelievers denounced and found strange, namely that trivial things should be used as examples, is not a fitting matter for denunciation or astonishment. This is because a parable (tamthil) is resorted to only for the clarity of meaning it provides, the lifting of the veil from the intended purpose, and the bringing of the imagined closer to the observed. If the one being illustrated is great, the thing used as illustration is likewise great; and if it is lowly, the thing used is likewise lowly. Thus, greatness or lowliness in the thing used as an example is nothing but a matter demanded by the state of the one being illustrated, which draws it toward itself, so the one who coins the example acts according to that case. Do you not see that when the truth was clear, manifest and radiant, it was illustrated by light and luminosity, and when falsehood was of the opposite quality, it was illustrated by darkness? And since the state of the gods which the disbelievers made as rivals to God was no state lower or less contemptible than that, the spider's house was made its example in weakness and frailty, and they were made less than the fly and of lower rank, and the gnat was struck as an example for them, so whatever is below it is not denounced or deemed novel. No one said to the one who gave the example: "Be ashamed of illustrating them with a gnat," because he is correct in his illustration, right in his statement, driving the parable according to the case it strikes, and following the pattern of what it demands and calls for. And to show that the believers, whose custom is fairness, acting on justice and equity, and considering matters with the eye of reason, when they hear such an illustration, know that it is the truth against which doubt cannot pass, and the correct view around which error does not roam.

And that the disbelievers, whom ignorance has overcome in their minds, and whom usurpation has seized in their insight, so that they do not perceive or apply their minds, or who recognize that it is the truth but whose love of leadership, desire for familiarity and habit does not leave them to be fair, when they hear it they oppose and stubbornly deny it, judge it to be false, and confront it with rejection. And that this is the cause of the increase in the guidance of the believers and the immersion of the wicked in their error and misguidance. How strange of them that they denied this, when people have continually coined examples using animals, birds, creeping things, insects and vermin, and the proverbs of the Arabs are before them, circulating in their towns and deserts, in which they illustrated with the most contemptible things, saying: "More daring than an ant," "Bolder than a fly," "Hearing sharper than a tick," "Colder than a locust," "Weaker than a moth," and "More eating than a weevil." And about the gnat they said: "Weaker than a gnat," "More precious than the marrow of a gnat," and "You have burdened me with the marrow of a gnat." Examples were also coined in the Gospel with trivial things, such as darnel, bran, the mustard seed, the pebble, the termite, the worm, and the wasp. Illustration with these things and with things more contemptible than them is something whose soundness and correctness are not hidden from anyone with the least sense; but it is the habit of the one defeated and bewildered, who has no hold left on any proof, no clinging to any sign or persuasion, to resort, out of extreme confusion and inability to devise a stratagem, to rejecting the obvious and denying the straight, relying on obstinacy and sophistry when he finds nothing else to rely upon. It is narrated from al-Hasan and Qatadah: when God mentioned the fly and the spider in His Book and struck them as examples for the polytheists, the Jews laughed and said: "This is not what the speech of God resembles."

So God, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse.

Modesty (al-haya') is a change and breaking that befalls a person from fear of what would be reproached and blamed. Its derivation is from life (hayah).

It is said: "Haya al-rajul," just as it is said: "nasiya," "hasha," and "shazhiya al-faras" (when these limbs become ailing), the living being being regarded, because of the breaking and change that overtakes him, as one whose strength is reversed and whose life is diminished, as they said: "So-and-so perished from modesty (haya') at such a thing," "he died of modesty," "I saw ruin in his face from the intensity of modesty," "he melted from modesty," and "he froze in his place from embarrassment." If you say: how is it permissible to describe the Eternal, glory be to Him, with it, while He cannot be characterized with change, fear or blame? This is in the hadith of Salman, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Indeed God is Living and Generous; He is modest toward His servant when the servant raises his hands to Him, that He should return them empty until He places good in them." Say: it proceeds by way of illustration, like His leaving the servant disappointed, and that He does not return the hands of the one who asks empty of His gift, out of His generosity, by leaving aside what one who is ashamed would leave aside, namely the rejection of one in need, out of modesty before him. And likewise the meaning of His words: "Indeed God is not ashamed" (la yastahyi) means He does not abandon striking the example of the gnat, leaving it as one abandons something from which one who is ashamed would refrain because of its lowliness. It is also permissible that this expression occurs in the speech of the disbelievers, who said: "Is the Lord of Muhammad not ashamed to strike an example with the fly and the spider?" and so it came in the manner of counterpart and matching the answer to the question. This is a wonderful kind of their speech and a marvelous ornament, among which is the saying of Abu Tammam:

"Who will convey to all the offspring of Ya'rub
that I built the neighbor before the dwelling?"

And when a man testified before Shurayh, he said: "You are indeed loose in your testimony." The man said: "It has not been wrapped (lam tujaʿʿad) from me." He said: "May God keep your land," and accepted his testimony. So what permitted "building the neighbor" and "wrapping the testimony" is the observance of counterpart. Were it not for building the house, "building the neighbor" would not be correct, and were it not for the testimony being loose, its wrapping would be impossible. How marvelous is the Revelation and its encompassing of the arts of eloquence and their branches; you will hardly find any art strange in it without finding it in its most upright methods and most firmly paved paths. Modesty has also been used metaphorically for what does not properly bear it:

"When they feel shy of the water presenting itself,
they drink with a leather bucket in a vessel of roses."

And he read (yastahi) with one yā' according to Ibn Kathir in the narration of Shibl. There are two usages: transitivity with the preposition and transitivity directly. They say: "istahyitu minhu" and "istahyitu-hu," and both are possible here.

As for "darb al-mathal" (striking an example): it is its making and fashioning, from "darb al-labin" (forming bricks) and "darb al-khatim" (striking a ring). In the hadith: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, struck a ring of gold." And "ma" here is indefinite (ibhamiyyah), which is the one which, when attached to an indefinite noun, makes it vague and increases it in generality and comprehensiveness, as when you say: "Give me a book, any," meaning whatever book it may be; or it is superfluous for emphasis, like the one in His words: "for their breaking their covenant." As if it were said: "God is not ashamed to strike an example, truly or at all." This is when you put "baʿūḍatan" in the accusative. But if you put it in the nominative, then it is relative, its clause being the sentence, because the estimate is: "it is a gnat," and the first part of the sentence is omitted as in: "perfection upon the one who did well." Another good and beautiful aspect is that the "ma" carries the meaning of interrogation: when they recoiled from God's illustrating their idols with trivial things, He said: "Indeed God is not ashamed to strike for the rivals whatever things he wills as an example, trivial ones, let alone the gnat and what is above it," as one says: "So-and-so does not care what he gives: how much a dinar and two dinars." The meaning is: God may illustrate the rivals and the lowliness of their status by what has nothing smaller or less than it, such as the indivisible part, or by what only He, through His subtlety, can perceive because of its extreme tininess, or by the non-existent, as the Arabs say: "So-and-so is less than nothing in number." And the words of the Exalted touch on this: "Indeed God knows what they call upon besides Him of anything." This reading is attributed to Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajjaj, the most chewing of the Arabs upon wormwood and southernwood, and the one attested to for eloquence; and they used to liken beauty to him. I do not think he took this reading except in this direction, which corresponds to his eloquence. "Ba'ūḍatan" is in the accusative either as an explanatory appositive to "mathalan," or as the object of "yadrib," with "mathalan" as a circumstantial accusative preceding it, or both are accusative objects, so that "darab" takes the course of "ja'ala." The derivation of "ba'ūḍ" is from "al-ba'ḍ," which means cutting, like "al-biḍʿ" and "al-ʿaḍb." It is said: "ba'aḍahu al-ba'ūḍ" (the gnat bit him). And he recited:

"How excellent is the house of Abu Dithar
when some of the people fear some of them."

The intended meaning of the house is the mosquito-net that protects from gnats during summer nights for those inside it; Abu Dithar is the name of a man, and "dithar" is what is worn over clothes. It is said: "when some of the people fear the gnat's bite, i.e., its cut and sting." It may also be that the meaning is: the best refuge and shelter is the house of Abu Dithar, from whose evil some people fear others. In it is double meaning (tawriyah), which is among the wonders of speech. Derived from it is "ba'ḍ al-shay'," because he cut it from it. "Ba'ūḍ" originally is an adjective on the pattern of "fa'ūl," like "quṭūʿ," but it became a noun by predominance.

وَكَذَلِكَ **الخَمُوش**[^1] ﴿فَمَا فَوْقَهَا﴾ فِيهِ مَعْنَيَانِ: أَحَدُهُمَا: فَمَا تَجَاوَزَهَا وَزَادَ عَلَيْهَا فِي الْمَعْنَى الَّذِي ضُرِبَتْ فِيهِ مَثَلًا، وَهُوَ الْقِلَّةُ وَالْحَقَارَةُ، نَحْوَ قَوْلِكَ لِمَنْ يَقُولُ: فُلَانٌ أَسْفَلُ النَّاسِ وَأَنْذَلُهُمْ: هُوَ فَوْقَ ذَاكَ، تُرِيدُ هُوَ أَبْلَغُ وَأَعْرَقُ فِيمَا وُصِفَ بِهِ مِنَ السَّفَالَةِ وَالنَّذَالَةِ. وَالثَّانِي: فَمَا زَادَ عَلَيْهَا فِي الْحَجْمِ، كَأَنَّهُ قَصَدَ بِذَلِكَ رَدَّ مَا اسْتَنْكَرُوهُ مِنْ ضَرْبِ الْمَثَلِ بِالذُّبَابِ وَالْعَنْكَبُوتِ، لِأَنَّهُمَا أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْبَعُوضَةِ. كَمَا تَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِكَ، وَقَدْ ذَمَّ مَنْ عَرَفْتَهُ يَشِحُّ بِأَدْنَى شَيْءٍ، فَقَالَ: فُلَانٌ بَخِلَ بِالدِّرْهَمِ وَالدِّرْهَمَيْنِ: هُوَ لَا يُبَالِي أَنْ يَبْخَلَ بِنِصْفِ دِرْهَمٍ فَمَا فَوْقَهُ، تُرِيدُ بِمَا فَوْقَهُ مَا بَخِلَ فِيهِ وَهُوَ الدِّرْهَمُ وَالدِّرْهَمَانِ، كَأَنَّكَ قُلْتَ: فَضْلًا عَنِ الدِّرْهَمِ وَالدِّرْهَمَيْنِ. وَنَحْوُهُ فِي الِاحْتِمَالَيْنِ مَا سَمِعْنَاهُ فِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنِ الْأَسْوَدِ قَالَ: دَخَلَ شَبَابٌ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ عَلَى عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا وَهِيَ بِمِنًى وَهُمْ يَضْحَكُونَ. فَقَالَتْ: مَا يُضْحِكُكُمْ؟ قَالُوا: فُلَانٌ خَرَّ عَلَى طُنُبِ فُسْطَاطٍ فَكَادَتْ عُنُقُهُ أَوْ عَيْنُهُ أَنْ تَذْهَبَ. فَقَالَتْ: لَا تَضْحَكُوا. إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ (ﷺ) قَالَ: «مَا مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ يُشَاكُ شَوْكَةً فَمَا فَوْقَهَا إِلَّا كُتِبَتْ لَهُ بِهَا دَرَجَةٌ وَمُحِيَتْ بِهَا عَنْهُ خَطِيئَةٌ»[^2]. يَحْتَمِلُ: فَمَا عَدَا الشَّوْكَةَ وَتَجَاوَزَهَا فِي الْقِلَّةِ، وَهِيَ نَحْوُ نُخْبَةِ النَّمْلَةِ فِي قَوْلِهِ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ: «مَا أَصَابَ الْمُؤْمِنَ مِنْ مَكْرُوهٍ فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لِخَطَايَاهُ حَتَّى نُخْبَةُ النَّمْلَةِ»[^3]، وَهِيَ عَضَّتُهَا. وَيَحْتَمِلُ مَا هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنَ الشَّوْكَةِ وَأَوْجَعُ، كَالْخُرُورِ عَلَى طُنُبِ الْفُسْطَاطِ. فَإِنْ قُلْتَ: كَيْفَ يُضْرَبُ الْمَثَلُ بِمَا دُونَ الْبَعُوضَةِ وَهِيَ النِّهَايَةُ فِي الصِّغَرِ؟ قُلْتُ: لَيْسَ كَذَلِكَ، فَإِنَّ جَنَاحَ الْبَعُوضَةِ أَقَلُّ مِنْهَا وَأَصْغَرُ بِدَرَجَاتٍ، وَقَدْ ضَرَبَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) مَثَلًا لِلدُّنْيَا[^4]، وَفِي خَلْقِ اللَّهِ حَيَوَانٌ أَصْغَرُ مِنْهَا وَمِنْ جَنَاحِهَا، رُبَّمَا رَأَيْتَ فِي تَضَاعِيفِ الْكُتُبِ الْعَتِيقَةِ دُوَيْبَّةً لَا يَكَادُ يُجَلِّيهَا لِلْبَصَرِ الْحَادِّ إِلَّا تَحَرُّكُهَا، فَإِذَا سَكَنَتْ فَالسُّكُونُ يُوَارِيهَا، ثُمَّ إِذَا لَوَّحْتَ لَهَا بِيَدِكَ حَادَتْ عَنْهَا وَتَجَنَّبَتْ مَضَرَّتَهَا، فَسُبْحَانَ مَنْ يُدْرِكُ صُورَةَ تِلْكَ وَأَعْضَاءَهَا الظَّاهِرَةَ وَالْبَاطِنَةَ وَتَفَاصِيلَ خِلْقَتِهَا وَيُبْصِرُ بَصَرَهَا وَيَطَّلِعُ عَلَى ضَمِيرِهَا، وَلَعَلَّ فِي خَلْقِهِ مَا هُوَ أَصْغَرُ مِنْهَا وَأَصْغَرُ ﴿Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows and of themselves and of what they do not know﴾. وَأَنْشَدْتُ لِبَعْضِهِمْ:

يَا مَنْ يَرَى مَدَّ البَعُوضِ جَنَاحَهَا ... فِي ظُلْمَةِ اللَّيْلِ البَهِيمِ الأَلْيَلِ
وَيَرَى عُرُوقَ نِيَاطِهَا فِي نَحْرِهَا ... وَالمُخَّ فِي تِلْكَ العِظَامِ النَّحَّلِ
اغْفِرْ لِعَبْدٍ تَابَ مِنْ فَرَطَاتِهِ ... مَا كَانَ مِنْهُ فِي الزَّمَانِ الأَوَّلِ[^5]

وَ**فَأَمَّا** حَرْفٌ فِيهِ مَعْنَى الشَّرْطِ، وَلِذَلِكَ يُجَابُ بِالْفَاءِ. وَفَائِدَتُهُ فِي الْكَلَامِ أَنْ يُعْطِيَهُ فَضْلَ تَوْكِيدٍ. تَقُولُ: زَيْدٌ ذَاهِبٌ. فَإِذَا قَصَدْتَ تَوْكِيدَ ذَاكَ، وَأَنَّهُ لَا مَحَالَةَ ذَاهِبٌ، وَأَنَّهُ بِصَدَدِ الذَّهَابِ، وَأَنَّهُ مِنْهُ عَزِيمَةٌ، قُلْتَ: أَمَّا زَيْدٌ فَذَاهِبٌ. وَلِذَلِكَ قَالَ سِيبَوَيْهِ فِي تَفْسِيرِهِ: مَهْمَا يَكُنْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَزَيْدٌ ذَاهِبٌ. وَهَذَا التَّفْسِيرُ مُدِلٌّ لِفَائِدَتَيْنِ: بَيَانِ كَوْنِهِ تَوْكِيدًا، وَأَنَّهُ فِي مَعْنَى الشَّرْطِ. فَفِي إِيرَادِ الْجُمْلَتَيْنِ مُصَدَّرَتَيْنِ بِهِ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يُقَلْ: فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَعْلَمُونَ، وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يَقُولُونَ، إِحْمَادٌ عَظِيمٌ لِأَمْرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَاعْتِدَادٌ بِعِلْمِهِمْ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ، وَنَعْيٌ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ إِغْفَالَهُمْ حَظَّهُمْ وَعِنَادَهُمْ وَرَمْيَهُمْ بِالْكَلِمَةِ الْحَمْقَاءِ. وَ**الْحَقُّ** الثَّابِتُ الَّذِي لَا يَسُوغُ إِنْكَارُهُ. يُقَالُ: حَقَّ الْأَمْرُ، إِذَا ثَبَتَ وَوَجَبَ. ﴿وَحَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ﴾[^6]، وَثَوْبٌ مُحَقَّقٌ: مُحْكَمُ النَّسْجِ. وَ**مَاذَا** فِيهِ وَجْهَانِ: أَنْ يَكُونَ «ذَا» اسْمًا مَوْصُولًا بِمَعْنَى «الَّذِي»، فَيَكُونَ كَلِمَتَيْنِ. وَأَنْ يَكُونَ «ذَا» مُرَكَّبَةً مَعَ «مَا» مَجْعُولَتَيْنِ اسْمًا وَاحِدًا فَتَكُونَ كَلِمَةً وَاحِدَةً، فَهُوَ عَلَى الْوَجْهِ الْأَوَّلِ مَرْفُوعُ الْمَحَلِّ عَلَى الِابْتِدَاءِ وَخَبَرُهُ «ذَا» مَعَ صِلَتِهِ. وَعَلَى الثَّانِي مَنْصُوبُ الْمَحَلِّ فِي حُكْمِ «مَا» وَحْدَهُ لَوْ قُلْتَ: مَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ. وَالْأَصْوَبُ فِي جَوَابِهِ أَنْ يَجِيءَ عَلَى الْأَوَّلِ مَرْفُوعًا، وَعَلَى الثَّانِي مَنْصُوبًا، لِيُطَابِقَ الْجَوَابُ السُّؤَالَ. وَقَدْ جَوَّزُوا عَكْسَ ذَلِكَ، تَقُولُ فِي جَوَابِ مَنْ قَالَ: مَا رَأَيْتَ؟ خَيْرٌ، أَيِ الْمَرْئِيُّ خَيْرٌ. وَفِي جَوَابِ: مَاذَا الَّذِي رَأَيْتَ؟ خَيْرًا، أَيْ رَأَيْتُ خَيْرًا. وَقُرِئَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ قُلِ الْعَفْوَ﴾[^7] بِالرَّفْعِ وَالنَّصْبِ عَلَى التَّقْدِيرَيْنِ. وَ**الْإِرَادَةُ** نَقِيضُ الْكَرَاهَةِ، وَهِيَ مَصْدَرُ أَرَدْتُ الشَّيْءَ إِذَا طَلَبَتْهُ نَفْسُكَ وَمَالَ إِلَيْهِ قَلْبُكَ. وَفِي حُدُودِ الْمُتَكَلِّمِينَ: الْإِرَادَةُ مَعْنًى يُوجِبُ لِلْحَيِّ حَالًا لِأَجْلِهَا يَقَعُ مِنْهُ الْفِعْلُ عَلَى وَجْهٍ دُونَ وَجْهٍ. وَقَدِ اخْتَلَفُوا فِي إِرَادَةِ اللَّهِ، فَبَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى أَنَّ لِلْبَارِئِ مِثْلَ صِفَةِ الْمُرِيدِ مِنَّا الَّتِي هِيَ الْقَصْدُ، وَهُوَ أَمْرٌ زَائِدٌ عَلَى كَوْنِهِ عَالِمًا غَيْرَ سَاهٍ. وَبَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى أَنَّ مَعْنَى إِرَادَتِهِ لِأَفْعَالِهِ هُوَ أَنَّهُ فَعَلَهَا وَهُوَ غَيْرُ سَاهٍ وَلَا مُكْرَهٍ. وَمَعْنَى إِرَادَتِهِ لِأَفْعَالِ غَيْرِهِ أَنَّهُ أَمَرَ بِهَا. وَالضَّمِيرُ فِي ﴿أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ﴾ لِلْمَثَلِ، أَوْ لِأَنْ يُضْرَبَ. وَفِي قَوْلِهِمْ: ﴿مَاذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِهَذَا مَثَلًا﴾ اسْتِرْذَالٌ وَاسْتِحْقَارٌ، كَمَا قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا فِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِي[^8]: يَا عَجَبًا لِابْنِ عَمْرٍو هَذَا؟ «**مَثَلًا**» نُصِبَ عَلَى التَّمْيِيزِ، كَقَوْلِكَ لِمَنْ أَجَابَ بِجَوَابٍ غَثٍّ: مَاذَا أَرَدْتَ بِهَذَا جَوَابًا؟ وَلِمَنْ حَمَلَ سِلَاحًا رَدِيئًا: كَيْفَ تَنْتَفِعُ بِهَذَا سِلَاحًا؟ أَوْ عَلَى الْحَالِ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿هَذِهِ نَاقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً﴾[^9]. وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿يُضِلُّ بِهِ كَثِيرًا وَيَهْدِي بِهِ كَثِيرًا﴾ جَاءَ مَجْرَى التَّفْسِيرِ وَالْبَيَانِ لِلْجُمْلَتَيْنِ الْمُصَدَّرَتَيْنِ بِ«أَمَّا»، وَأَنَّ فَرِيقَ الْعَالِمِينَ بِأَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ وَفَرِيقَ الْجَاهِلِينَ الْمُسْتَهْزِئِينَ بِهِ كِلَاهُمَا مَوْصُوفٌ بِالْكَثْرَةِ، وَأَنَّ الْعِلْمَ بِكَوْنِهِ حَقًّا مِنْ بَابِ الْهُدَى الَّذِي ازْدَادَ بِهِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ نُورًا إِلَى نُورِهِمْ، وَأَنَّ الْجَهْلَ بِحُسْنِ مَوْرِدِهِ مِنْ بَابِ الضَّلَالَةِ الَّتِي زَادَتِ الْجَهَلَةَ خَبْطًا فِي ظُلْمَائِهِمْ. فَإِنْ قُلْتَ: لِمَ وُصِفَ الْمَهْدِيُّونَ بِالْكَثْرَةِ وَالْقِلَّةُ صِفَتُهُمْ[^10]؟ قُلْتُ: أَهْلُ الْهُدَى كَثِيرٌ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ، وَحِينَ يُوصَفُونَ بِالْقِلَّةِ إِنَّمَا يُوصَفُونَ بِهَا بِالْقِيَاسِ إِلَى أَهْلِ الضَّلَالِ. وَأَيْضًا فَإِنَّ الْقَلِيلَ مِنَ الْمَهْدِيِّينَ كَثِيرٌ فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ وَإِنْ قَلُّوا فِي الصُّورَةِ، فَسُمُّوا ذَهَابًا إِلَى الْحَقِيقَةِ كَثِيرًا:

إِنَّ الكِرَامَ كَثِيرٌ فِي البِلَادِ وَإِنْ ... قَلُّوا كَمَا غَيْرُهُمْ قَلَّ وَإِنْ كَثُرُوا[^11]

وَ﴿قَلِيلٌ مِنْ عِبَادِيَ الشَّكُورُ﴾[^12]، ﴿وَقَلِيلٌ مَا هُمْ﴾[^13]. النَّاسُ كَإِبِلٍ مِائَةٍ لَا تَجِدُ فِيهَا رَاحِلَةً. وَجَدْتَ النَّاسَ أَخْبَرَ تَقْلُهُ؟

وَإِسْنَادُ الْإِضْلَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى إِسْنَادُ الْفِعْلِ إِلَى السَّبَبِ[^14]: لِأَنَّهُ لَمَّا ضَرَبَ الْمَثَلَ فَضَلَّ بِهِ قَوْمٌ وَاهْتَدَى بِهِ قَوْمٌ، تَسَبَّبَ لِضَلَالِهِمْ وَهُدَاهُمْ. وَعَنْ مَالِكِ بْنِ دِينَارٍ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ دَخَلَ عَلَى مَحْبُوسٍ قَدْ أُخِذَ بِمَالٍ عَلَيْهِ وَقُيِّدَ، فَقَالَ: يَا أَبَا يَحْيَى، أَمَا تَرَى مَا نَحْنُ فِيهِ مِنَ الْقُيُودِ؟ فَرَفَعَ مَالِكٌ رَأْسَهُ فَرَأَى سَلَّةً. فَقَالَ: لِمَنْ هَذِهِ السَّلَّةُ؟ فَقَالَ: لِي، فَأَمَرَ بِهَا تُنْزَلُ، فَإِذَا دَجَاجٌ وَأَخْبِصَةٌ، فَقَالَ مَالِكٌ: هَذِهِ وَضَعَتِ الْقُيُودَ عَلَى رِجْلِكَ. وَقَرَأَ زَيْدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: ﴿يَضِلُّ بِهِ كَثِيرًا﴾[^15]. وَكَذَلِكَ: ﴿وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِ إِلَّا الْفَاسِقِينَ﴾[^16]. وَ**الْفِسْقُ**: الْخُرُوجُ عَنِ الْقَصْدِ. قَالَ رُؤْبَةُ:

فَوَاسِقًا عَنْ قَصْدِهَا جَوَائِرَا[^17]

وَ**الْفَاسِقُ** فِي الشَّرِيعَةِ: الْخَارِجُ عَنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ بِارْتِكَابِ الْكَبِيرَةِ، وَهُوَ النَّازِلُ بَيْنَ الْمَنْزِلَتَيْنِ[^18] أَيْ بَيْنَ مَنْزِلَةِ الْمُؤْمِنِ وَالْكَافِرِ، وَقَالُوا: إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَنْ حَدَّ لَهُ هَذَا الْحَدَّ: أَبُو حُذَيْفَةَ وَاصِلُ بْنُ عَطَاءٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ وَعَنْ أَشْيَاعِهِ[^19]. وَكَوْنُهُ بَيْنَ بَيْنَ أَنَّ حُكْمَهُ حُكْمُ الْمُؤْمِنِ فِي أَنَّهُ يُنَاكَحُ وَيُوَارَثُ وَيُغَسَّلُ وَيُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ وَيُدْفَنُ فِي مَقَابِرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ. وَهُوَ كَالْكَافِرِ فِي الذَّمِّ وَاللَّعْنِ وَالْبَرَاءَةِ مِنْهُ وَاعْتِقَادِ عَدَاوَتِهِ، وَأَنْ لَا تُقْبَلَ لَهُ شَهَادَةٌ. وَمَذْهَبُ مَالِكِ بْنِ أَنَسٍ وَالزَّيْدِيَّةِ[^20]: أَنَّ الصَّلَاةَ لَا تُجْزِئُ خَلْفَهُ. وَيُقَالُ لِلْخُلَفَاءِ الْمَرَدَةِ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ: الْفَسَقَةُ. وَقَدْ جَاءَ الِاسْتِعْمَالَانِ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: ﴿بِئْسَ الِاسْمُ الْفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ الْإِيمَانِ﴾[^21] يُرِيدُ اللَّمْزَ وَالتَّنَابُزَ، ﴿إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ﴾[^22].

**النَّقْضُ**: الْفَسْخُ وَفَكُّ التَّرْكِيبِ. فَإِنْ قُلْتَ: مِنْ أَيْنَ سَاغَ اسْتِعْمَالُ النَّقْضِ فِي إِبْطَالِ الْعَهْدِ؟ قُلْتُ: مِنْ حَيْثُ تَسْمِيَتُهُمُ الْعَهْدَ بِالْحَبْلِ عَلَى سَبِيلِ **الِاسْتِعَارَةِ**[^23]، لِمَا فِيهِ مِنْ ثَبَاتِ الْوُصْلَةِ بَيْنَ الْمُتَعَاهِدَيْنِ. وَمِنْهُ قَوْلُ ابْنِ التَّيِّهَانِ فِي بَيْعَةِ الْعَقَبَةِ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ حِبَالًا وَنَحْنُ قَاطِعُوهَا، فَنَخْشَى إِنْ أَعَزَّكَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَأَظْهَرَكَ أَنْ تَرْجِعَ إِلَى قَوْمِكَ»[^24]. وَهَذَا مِنْ أَسْرَارِ الْبَلَاغَةِ وَلَطَائِفِهَا أَنْ يَسْكُتُوا عَنْ ذِكْرِ الشَّيْءِ الْمُسْتَعَارِ، ثُمَّ يَرْمُزُوا إِلَيْهِ بِذِكْرِ شَيْءٍ مِنْ رَوَادِفِهِ، فَيُنَبِّهُوا بِتِلْكَ الرَّمْزَةِ عَلَى مَكَانِهِ. وَنَحْوُهُ قَوْلُكَ: شُجَاعٌ يَفْتَرِسُ أَقْرَانَهُ، وَعَالِمٌ يَغْتَرِفُ مِنْهُ النَّاسُ، وَإِذَا تَزَوَّجْتَ امْرَأَةً فَاسْتَوْثِرْهَا. لَمْ تَقُلْ هَذَا إِلَّا وَقَدْ نَبَّهْتَ عَلَى الشُّجَاعِ وَالْعَالِمِ بِأَنَّهُمَا أَسَدٌ وَبَحْرٌ، وَعَلَى الْمَرْأَةِ بِأَنَّهَا فِرَاشٌ[^25]. وَ**الْعَهْدُ**: الْمُوَثَّقُ. وَعَهِدَ إِلَيْهِ فِي كَذَا: إِذَا وَصَّاهُ بِهِ وَوَثَّقَهُ عَلَيْهِ. وَاسْتَعْهَدَ مِنْهُ: إِذَا اشْتَرَطَ عَلَيْهِ وَاسْتَوْثَقَ مِنْهُ. وَالْمُرَادُ بِهَؤُلَاءِ النَّاقِضِينَ لِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ: أَحْبَارُ الْيَهُودِ الْمُتَعَنِّتُونَ، أَوْ مُنَافِقُوهُمْ، أَوِ الْكُفَّارُ جَمِيعًا. فَإِنْ قُلْتَ: فَمَا الْمُرَادُ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ؟ قُلْتُ: مَا رُكِزَ فِي عُقُولِهِمْ مِنَ الْحُجَّةِ عَلَى التَّوْحِيدِ، كَأَنَّهُ أَمَرَ وَصَّاهُمْ بِهِ وَوَثَّقَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ، وَهُوَ مَعْنَى قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى﴾[^26]. أَوْ أَخْذُ الْمِيثَاقِ عَلَيْهِمْ بِأَنَّهُمْ إِذَا بُعِثَ إِلَيْهِمْ رَسُولٌ يُصَدِّقُهُ اللَّهُ بِمُعْجِزَاتِهِ صَدَّقُوهُ وَاتَّبَعُوهُ، وَلَمْ يَكْتُمُوا ذِكْرَهُ فِيمَا تَقَدَّمَهُ مِنَ الْكُتُبِ الْمُنَزَّلَةِ عَلَيْهِمْ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِي أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ﴾[^27]. وَقَوْلُهُ فِي الْإِنْجِيلِ لِعِيسَى صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ: «سَأُنَزِّلُ عَلَيْكَ كِتَابًا فِيهِ نَبَأُ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ، وَمَا أَرَيْتُهُ إِيَّاهُمْ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ، وَمَا أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَا نَقَضُوا مِنْ مِيثَاقِهِمُ الَّذِي وَاثَقُوا بِهِ، وَمَا ضَيَّعُوا مِنْ عَهْدِهِ إِلَيْهِمْ». وَحُسْنُ صُنْعِهِ لِلَّذِينَ قَامُوا بِمِيثَاقِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى وَأَوْفَوْا بِعَهْدِهِ، وَنَصْرُهُ إِيَّاهُمْ، وَكَيْفَ أَنْزَلَ بَأْسَهُ وَنِقْمَتَهُ بِالَّذِينَ غَدَرُوا وَنَقَضُوا مِيثَاقَهُمْ وَلَمْ يُوفُوا بِعَهْدِهِ، لِأَنَّ الْيَهُودَ فَعَلُوا بِاسْمِ عِيسَى مَا فَعَلُوا بِاسْمِ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمَا وَسَلَّمَ مِنَ التَّحْرِيفِ وَالْجُحُودِ وَكَفَرُوا بِهِ كَمَا كَفَرُوا بِمُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ. وَقِيلَ: هُوَ أَخْذُ اللَّهِ الْعَهْدَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَنْ لَا يَسْفِكُوا دِمَاءَهُمْ، وَلَا يَبْغِيَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ، وَلَا يَقْطَعُوا أَرْحَامَهُمْ. وَقِيلَ: عَهْدُ اللَّهِ إِلَى خَلْقِهِ ثَلَاثَةُ عُهُودٍ: الْعَهْدُ الْأَوَّلُ الَّذِي أَخَذَهُ عَلَى جَمِيعِ ذُرِّيَّةِ آدَمَ، الْإِقْرَارُ بِرُبُوبِيَّتِهِ[^28] وَهُوَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ﴾[^29]، وَعَهْدٌ خُصَّ بِهِ النَّبِيُّونَ أَنْ يُبَلِّغُوا الرِّسَالَةَ وَيُقِيمُوا الدِّينَ وَلَا يَتَفَرَّقُوا فِيهِ، وَهُوَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مِيثَاقَهُمْ﴾[^30]، وَعَهْدٌ خُصَّ بِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ وَهُوَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَكْتُمُونَهُ﴾[^31]. وَالضَّمِيرُ فِي «مِيثَاقِهِ» لِلْعَهْدِ، وَهُوَ مَا وَثَّقُوا بِهِ عَهْدَ اللَّهِ مِنْ قَبُولِهِ وَإِلْزَامِهِ أَنْفُسَهُمْ. وَيَجُوزُ أَنْ يَكُونَ بِمَعْنَى تَوْثِقَتِهِ، كَمَا أَنَّ الْمِيعَادَ وَالْمِيلَادَ بِمَعْنَى الْوَعْدِ وَالْوِلَادَةِ. وَيَجُوزُ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ الضَّمِيرُ إِلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى، أَيْ مِنْ بَعْدِ تَوْثِقَتِهِ عَلَيْهِمْ، أَوْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا وَثَّقَ بِهِ عَهْدَهُ مِنْ آيَاتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَإِنْذَارِ رُسُلِهِ. وَمَعْنَى قَطْعِهِمْ مَا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُوصَلَ: قَطْعُهُمُ الْأَرْحَامَ وَمُوَالَاةَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَقِيلَ قَطْعُهُمْ مَا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ مِنَ الْوُصْلَةِ وَالِاتِّحَادِ وَالِاجْتِمَاعِ عَلَى الْحَقِّ، فِي إِيمَانِهِمْ بِبَعْضٍ وَكُفْرِهِمْ بِبَعْضٍ. فَإِنْ قُلْتَ: مَا الْأَمْرُ؟ قُلْتُ:

Seeking an act from one who is beneath you and urging him to it. From this is named the matter (al-amr), which is the singular of "affairs" (al-umur), because the call which summons the one who undertakes it resembles a commander who orders him to do it; so it is said of it "amr," naming the object by the verbal noun, as if it were "ma'mur bihi" (that which is commanded). Likewise it is called "sha'n." The sha'n is the seeking and the intention. It is said: "sha'antu sha'nahu," meaning, I intended his intention.

﴿They are the losers﴾, because they exchanged breaking for fulfilment, severing for joining, and corruption for righteousness, and its punishment for its reward.

The meaning of the hamza in "kayfa" (how) is similar to its meaning in your saying: "Do you disbelieve in God, when with you is that which turns you away from disbelief and calls you to faith?" It is rebuke and wonder (inkar wa-ta'ajjub). Its parallel is your saying: "Do you fly without wings?" and "How can you fly without wings?" If you say: your saying "Do you fly without wings?" is a denial of flying, since it is impossible without wings, whereas disbelief is not impossible given what was mentioned of causing to die and giving life. I say: it has been brought out in the form of the impossible because of the strength of what turns away from disbelief and calls to faith. If you say: it has become clear what the hamza is, that it is for denying the act and announcing its impossibility in itself, or for the strength of what turns away from it, so what do you say about "kayfa" when it is a denial of the state in which their disbelief occurs? I say: the state of a thing follows its essence, so when the existence of the essence is impossible, the existence of the state is impossible too. Thus the denial of the state of disbelief is, because the state follows the essence of disbelief and accompanies it, a denial of the essence of disbelief, and its establishment is by way of metonymy (kinaya), and that is stronger and more eloquent in denying disbelief. Its clarification: if one denies that their disbelief has a state in which it exists, and it is known that every existent does not separate from a state and attribute when it exists, and it is impossible that it exists without any attribute, then this is a denial of its existence by way of demonstrative proof (al-tariq al-burhani).

The waw in His saying "wa-kuntum amwatan" (while you were dead) is for the state (hal). If you say: how is it correct that it be a state while it is past, and one does not say "I came and the amir had come" but rather "wa-qad qama" (with qad), unless qad is implied? I say: the waw did not enter upon "kuntum amwatan" alone, but upon the whole sentence from "kuntum amwatan" to "turja'un" (you will be returned), as if it were said: "How do you disbelieve in God while your affair is this and your condition is that you were dead, sperm-drops in the loins of your fathers, then He made you alive, then He will cause you to die after this life, then He will give you life after death, then He will call you to account." If you say: part of the story is past and part is future, and neither the past nor the future can be a state unless it is a present act at the time of what it is a state of, so what is the present that became a state? I say: it is the knowledge of the story, as if it were said: "How do you disbelieve while you know this story, from its beginning to its end?" If you say: then the meaning returns to your saying: "In what state do you disbelieve while you know this story?" so what is the correctness of this? I say: we have mentioned that the meaning of the interrogation in "kayfa" is denial, and that the denial of the state includes the denial of the essence by way of metonymy. So it is as if it were said: "How strange is your disbelief with your knowledge of this condition of yours!" If you say: if their knowledge was connected to their having been dead and then His giving them life, then He will cause them to die, why is it not connected to the second giving of life and the return? I say: they were able to know both by the proofs that lead to it, so that was in the position of having knowledge. Many of them knew and then were obstinate. The "amwat" is the plural of "mayyit," like the plural "aqyal" of "qayl" [[His saying "like the plural of qayl": Qayl is a king of the kings of Himyar. Its origin is "qayl" with shadda. Whoever pluralizes it as "aqyal" does not treat its origin as doubled. Thus in al-Sihah. (Gh.)]]. If you say: how is it said to them "amwat" while they are inanimate, when "mayyit" is said only of what can be characterized by life among living beings? I say: rather, it is said of one lacking life, as in His saying: "a dead land" (baldatan mayta), "and a sign for them is the dead earth" (al-ardu al-mayyita), "dead, not living" (amwatun ghayru ahya'). It is also permissible that it be a metaphor, because both share that there is no spirit and no sensation.

If you say: what is meant by the second giving of life? I say: it is permissible that it means giving life in the grave, and by the return: the resurrection (nushur). And it may mean the resurrection, and by the return: the arrival at recompense. If you say: why was the first conjunction with fa' and the consequence with thumma? I say: because the first giving of life followed death without delay, whereas death was delayed from the giving of life. The second giving of life is likewise delayed from death, if what is meant is the resurrection, with an evident delay. If what is meant is giving life in the grave, then knowledge of its delay is gained from it, and the return to recompense is also delayed from the resurrection. If you say: from where comes the denial of the combination of disbelief with the story God mentioned: is it because it contains clear signs that turn them away from disbelief, or because of great blessings which deserve to be thanked and not disbelieved? I say: both are possible together, because what He enumerated are signs, and they, being signs, are among the greatest blessings. "For you" (lakum): for your sake and for your benefit in your worldly life and your religion. The worldly benefit is evident. As for the religious benefit: reflection on it and the wonders of creation in it which point to the Creator, the Powerful, the Wise, and the reminder in it of the Hereafter and its reward and punishment, since it contains causes of comfort and pleasure in various foods, drinks, fruits, marriages, vehicles, and beautiful pleasing sights, and causes of dread and hardship in kinds of hateful things such as fires, thunderbolts, beasts, vermin, poisonous winds, griefs and fears. It has been argued from His saying "He created for you" that things which can be benefited from, and which do not operate like prohibitions in reason, were created in origin permissible absolutely for anyone to take and benefit from. If you say: is there any correctness to the view of one who claims that the meaning is "He created for you the earth and what is in it"?

I say: if by "the earth" is meant the lower directions, not the dusty ground, as "the heaven" is mentioned and the upper directions are meant, that is permissible, since the dusty ground and what is in it lie in the lower directions. "Jami'an" (all) is in the accusative as a state from the second relative pronoun. "Istiwa'" means uprightness and straightness. It is said: "istawa al-'ud" (the stick became straight) when it stood and became upright; then it was said "istawa ilayhi" like an arrow released when it aims at it directly, without turning aside to anything. From this is borrowed His saying: "Then He istawa to the heaven," meaning He directed Himself to it by His will and purpose after creating what is in the earth, without intending in between to create anything else. "The heaven" means the upper directions, as if it were said: "Then He turned upward." The pronoun in "fa-sawwahunna" is an ambiguous pronoun, and "sab'a samawat" (seven heavens) explains it, like the saying "rabbahu rajulan" (his lord, a man). It is said the pronoun refers to the heaven, and "al-sama'" has the sense of a genus. It is also said it is the plural of "sama'a," but the Arabic way is the first. The meaning of "taswiyatuhunna" is the proportioning of their creation, its precedence, and its freedom from crookedness and fissures, or the completion of their creation. "And He is, of everything, Knowing": therefore He created them as a uniform, firm creation without disparity, along with creating what is in the earth according to the needs, benefits and interests of its inhabitants.

If you say: what you explained the "istiwa'" toward the heaven by is contradicted by "thumma," because it gives the sense of delay and interval? I say: "thumma" here is for the difference between the two creations and the excellence of the creation of the heavens over the creation of the earth, not for delay in time, as in His saying: "then he was among those who believed." Moreover, even if it were for delay in time, what you objected to would not follow, because the meaning is that when He intended the heaven, He did not create anything else in between—that is, in the course of that intention toward it. I say: no, because the body of the earth was created before the creation of the heaven, while its spreading out was later. It is rebuke and wonder (inkar wa-ta'ajjub). Its parallel is your saying: "Do you fly without wings?" and "How can you fly without wings?" If you say: your saying "Do you fly without wings?" is a denial of flying, since it is impossible without wings, whereas disbelief is not impossible given what was mentioned of causing to die and giving life. I say: it has been brought out in the form of the impossible because of the strength of what turns away from disbelief and calls to faith. If you say: it has become clear what the hamza is, that it is for denying the act and announcing its impossibility in itself, or for the strength of what turns away from it, so what do you say about "kayfa" when it is a denial of the state in which their disbelief occurs? I say: the state of a thing follows its essence, so when the existence of the essence is impossible, the existence of the state is impossible too. Thus the denial of the state of disbelief is, because the state follows the essence of disbelief and accompanies it, a denial of the essence of disbelief, and its establishment is by way of metonymy (kinaya), and that is stronger and more eloquent in denying disbelief. Its clarification: if one denies that their disbelief has a state in which it exists, and it is known that every existent does not separate from a state and attribute when it exists, and it is impossible that it exists without any attribute, then this is a denial of its existence by way of demonstrative proof (al-tariq al-burhani).

The waw in His saying "wa-kuntum amwatan" (while you were dead) is for the state (hal). If you say: how is it correct that it be a state while it is past, and one does not say "I came and the amir had come" but rather "wa-qad qama" (with qad), unless qad is implied? I say: the waw did not enter upon "kuntum amwatan" alone, but upon the whole sentence from "kuntum amwatan" to "turja'un" (you will be returned), as if it were said: "How do you disbelieve in God while your affair is this and your condition is that you were dead, sperm-drops in the loins of your fathers, then He made you alive, then He will cause you to die after this life, then He will give you life after death, then He will call you to account." If you say: part of the story is past and part is future, and neither the past nor the future can be a state unless it is a present act at the time of what it is a state of, so what is the present that became a state? I say: it is the knowledge of the story, as if it were said: "How do you disbelieve while you know this story, from its beginning to its end?" If you say: then the meaning returns to your saying: "In what state do you disbelieve while you know this story?" so what is the correctness of this? I say: we have mentioned that the meaning of the interrogation in "kayfa" is denial, and that the denial of the state includes the denial of the essence by way of metonymy. So it is as if it were said: "How strange is your disbelief with your knowledge of this condition of yours!" If you say: if their knowledge was connected to their having been dead and then His giving them life, then He will cause them to die, why is it not connected to the second giving of life and the return? I say: they were able to know both by the proofs that lead to it, so that was in the position of having knowledge. Many of them knew and then were obstinate. The "amwat" is the plural of "mayyit," like the plural "aqyal" of "qayl" [[His saying "like the plural of qayl": Qayl is a king of the kings of Himyar. Its origin is "qayl" with shadda. Whoever pluralizes it as "aqyal" does not treat its origin as doubled. Thus in al-Sihah. (Gh.)]]. If you say: how is it said to them "amwat" while they are inanimate, when "mayyit" is said only of what can be characterized by life among living beings? I say: rather, it is said of one lacking life, as in His saying: "a dead land" (baldatan mayta), "and a sign for them is the dead earth" (al-ardu al-mayyita), "dead, not living" (amwatun ghayru ahya'). It is also permissible that it be a metaphor, because both share that there is no spirit and no sensation.

If you say: what is meant by the second giving of life? I say: it is permissible that it means giving life in the grave, and by the return: the resurrection (nushur). And it may mean the resurrection, and by the return: the arrival at recompense. If you say: why was the first conjunction with fa' and the consequence with thumma? I say: because the first giving of life followed death without delay, whereas death was delayed from the giving of life. The second giving of life is likewise delayed from death, if what is meant is the resurrection, with an evident delay. If what is meant is giving life in the grave, then knowledge of its delay is gained from it, and the return to recompense is also delayed from the resurrection. If you say: from where comes the denial of the combination of disbelief with the story God mentioned: is it because it contains clear signs that turn them away from disbelief, or because of great blessings which deserve to be thanked and not disbelieved? I say: both are possible together, because what He enumerated are signs, and they, being signs, are among the greatest blessings. "For you" (lakum): for your sake and for your benefit in your worldly life and your religion. The worldly benefit is evident. As for the religious benefit: reflection on it and the wonders of creation in it which point to the Creator, the Powerful, the Wise, and the reminder in it of the Hereafter and its reward and punishment, since it contains causes of comfort and pleasure in various foods, drinks, fruits, marriages, vehicles, and beautiful pleasing sights, and causes of dread and hardship in kinds of hateful things such as fires, thunderbolts, beasts, vermin, poisonous winds, griefs and fears. If you say: is there any correctness to the view of one who claims that the meaning is "He created for you the earth and what is in it"?

I say: if by "the earth" is meant the lower directions, not the dusty ground, as "the heaven" is mentioned and the upper directions are meant, that is permissible, since the dusty ground and what is in it lie in the lower directions. It is said: "istawa al-'ud" (the stick became straight) when it stood and became upright; then it was said "istawa ilayhi" like an arrow released when it aims at it directly, without turning aside to anything. From this is borrowed His saying: "Then He istawa to the heaven," meaning He directed Himself to it by His will and purpose after creating what is in the earth, without intending in between to create anything else. **Translation of al-Zamakhshari's commentary (al-Kashshaf) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 30–33**

﴿And when your Lord said to the angels...﴾ *wa-idh* is in the accusative case, governed by an implied *udhkur* (remember). It may also be governed by *qalū* (they said).

*Al-malā'ika* (the angels) is the plural of *malak*, in its original form (*mal'ak*), like *shamā'il* being the plural of *shamal*. The affixing of the *tā'* marks the feminine plural.

*Jā'il* (appointing) derives from *ja'ala*, which takes two objects. It entered upon the subject and predicate, which are the phrase *fī al-ard khalīfa* (on the earth, a successor), so these two became its two objects.

Its meaning is "one who will make [someone] a successor on the earth." *Khalīfa* (successor) is one who succeeds another. The meaning is "a successor from among you," because they (the jinn, or earlier inhabitants) were the inhabitants of the earth, and Adam and his descendants succeeded them in it.

If you ask: why was it not said *khalā'if* or *khulafā'* (plural forms)?

I answer: by *khalīfa* is meant Adam, and by mentioning him they dispensed with mentioning his offspring, just as the mention of the ancestor of a tribe is sufficient in your saying *Muḍar* and *Hāshim*. Or it may mean "one who will succeed you," or "a successor who will succeed you," and so it is singular for this reason. It was also read *khalīqa* with a *qāf*.

It is also possible that the meaning is "a successor of Mine," because Adam was God's successor on His earth, and so is every prophet: ﴿Indeed We have made you a successor on the earth﴾ (38:26).

If you ask: for what purpose did He inform them of this?

I answer: so that they would ask that question and be answered with what they were answered, and thus know the wisdom in their being made successors before their existence, as a safeguard for them against the objection of doubt at the time of their succession. It was also said: to teach His servants consultation in their affairs before undertaking them, and presenting them to their trustworthy and sincere advisers, although He, by His knowledge and perfect wisdom, is independent of consultation.

﴿They said: Will You place in it one who will spread corruption therein and shed blood...﴾ *Ataj'alu* is an expression of astonishment that people of disobedience should be made successors in place of people of obedience, while He is the Wise who does only good and wills only good.

[[The words "He is the Wise who does only good" and what follows are according to the Mu'tazilites. As for the People of the Sunna, He, exalted is He, does good and evil and wills both. (ʿ)]]

If you ask: how did they know this, so as to be astonished by it, when it is unseen?

I answer: they knew it by information from God, or from the Preserved Tablet (*al-lawḥ*), or it was established in their knowledge that the angels alone are the infallible creation, and that every creation other than them does not share their attribute. Or they analogized one of the two species (humans and jinn) to the other, since they settled the earth and corrupted it before the angels dwelt there.

It was read *yasfiku* with a *ḍamma* on the *fā'*, *yusfaku*, *yasfuk* (from *asfaka*), and *safaka*.

The *wāw* in *wa-naḥnu* (while we) is for the circumstantial state, as you say: "Do you do good to so-and-so while I have more right to it than him?"

*Al-tasbīḥ* (glorification) is declaring God far from evil, and likewise *taqdīs* (sanctification), from *sabaḥa* (to swim/travel) in the earth and water, and *qaddasa* in the earth: when one goes off in it and gets far away.

*Bi-ḥamdika* (with Your praise) is in the position of a circumstantial state: that is, "we glorify You while praising You and linked with Your praise," because were it not for Your favour upon us with success and gentleness, we would not be able to worship You.

﴿I know what you do not know﴾: that is, I know of the benefits in this matter what is hidden from you.

If you ask: why did He not explain those benefits to them?

I answer: it suffices the servants to know that all the acts of God are good and wise, even if the aspect of goodness and wisdom is hidden from them. Moreover, He did explain some of it in what follows: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾ (2:31). And the derivation of "Ādam" from *adama* (the brown colour/skin) and from *adīm al-arḍ* (the surface of the earth) is like their derivation of "Yaʿqūb" from *ʿaqab* (heel), "Idrīs" from *dars* (study), and "Iblīs" from *iblās* (despair). *Ādam* is a non-Arabic name, and the closest form of it is that it is on the pattern *fāʿal*, like *Āzar*, *ʿĀzar*, *ʿĀbir*, *Shālikh*, *Fāligh*, and similar names.

﴿The names, all of them﴾: that is, the names of the named things (*al-musammayāt*).

[[Mahmud, may God have mercy on him, said: "that is, the names of the named things, etc." Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: He flees from the belief that the name is the named, because that is the belief of the People of the Sunna, so he devises a stratagem to remove it from the implication of the verse by his words ﴿Inform them of their names﴾ (2:33), and he ignores His words ﴿Then He presented them to the angels﴾ (2:31). The pronoun in it refers, by agreement, to the named things, and only the names have been mentioned, which shows that the names are the named things. He also turns away from the wisdom of teaching, and that its connection is to the very words, with no great purpose in it. Rather, the important purpose is teaching him the essences of the named things, and making him acquainted with their realities and with the properties and secrets that God has placed in them, and with their names too. For the way of teaching distinguishes each reality by its name. So it is established by these two points that the meaning of "the names" is "the named things." As for his argument from His words ﴿Inform Me of the names of these﴾ (2:31), its best result is the addition of the names to the essences. They may say: if the names were the essences, it would entail the addition of a thing to itself; but that is not a valid objection, for this addition is like its counterpart in your saying "the self of Zayd and his reality." So the meaning is then "inform Me of the realities of these," and there is no objection to this addition, for the names are in the sense of the named things. The realities are more general than "these" that are pointed to and the one added to, so the addition is valid because of the difference between the more general and the more specific; and this is what validates the addition in "the self of Zayd" and similar expressions.

So this is a sample of the question of the name and the named, specific to this verse. In it, God willing, is sufficiency. Although the theologians count it among the science of *kalām*, it is overwhelmingly a verbal question, in which the disagreement between the Ash'arites and the Mu'tazilites does not return, in terms of reality, to much.]]

The genitive complement was omitted because it is known and indicated by the mention of "the names," since a name must have a named thing. In its place the definite article *al-* was given, as in His words ﴿and the head has blazed with grey﴾ (19:4).

If you ask: why not claim that the genitive was omitted and the complement put in its place, the original being "and He taught Adam the named things of the names"?

I answer: because teaching had to be connected to the names, not to the named things, by His words ﴿Inform Me of the names of these﴾ (2:31), and ﴿Inform them of their names﴾ and ﴿So when he informed them of their names﴾ (2:33). Just as the informing was connected to the names and not to the named things (He did not say "inform Me of these" or "inform them of them"), so the teaching had to be connected to them.

If you ask: what then is the meaning of His teaching him the names of the named things?

I answer: He showed him the kinds He had created, and taught him that this one's name is "horse," this one's name is "camel," this one's name is so-and-so, and this one's name is so-and-so; and He taught him their states and what is connected to them of religious and worldly benefits.

﴿Then He presented them﴾: that is, He presented the named things. He used the masculine pronoun because among the named things there are rational beings, so the masculine prevailed.

He asked them to inform Him, knowing their inability to inform, as a rebuke: ﴿if you are truthful﴾ (2:31), meaning in your claim that I will appoint as successors on the earth those who corrupt and shed blood, intending thereby to refute them, and that among those whom He appoints there are the scientific benefits which are the foundations of all benefits, for which they deserve to be appointed as successors. Thus He showed them that, and explained to them some of what had been left general of the benefits in their appointment, in His words ﴿I know what you do not know﴾ (2:30). His words ﴿Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth?﴾ (2:33) recall His words to them ﴿I know what you do not know﴾, except that He expressed it in a more expansive and clearer manner.

It was read *wa-ʿullima Ādam* with the passive. ʿAbdullah read *ʿaraḍahunna* (them, feminine plural), and Ubayy read *ʿaraḍahā* (it). The meaning is "He presented their named things" or "its named things," because presentation is not valid for names.

It was read *Unabbīhim* with the *hamza* changed to *yā'* (*unabbīhim*), and *Anbihum* with it dropped, with the *hā'* kasra in both.

﴿And when your Lord said to the angels...﴾ *wa-idh* is in the accusative case, governed by an implied *udhkur* (remember). It may also be governed by *qalū* (they said).

*Al-malā'ika* (the angels) is the plural of *malak*, in its original form (*mal'ak*), like *shamā'il* being the plural of *shamal*. The affixing of the *tā'* marks the feminine plural.

*Jā'il* (appointing) derives from *ja'ala*, which takes two objects. It entered upon the subject and predicate, which are the phrase *fī al-ard khalīfa* (on the earth, a successor), so these two became its two objects.

Its meaning is "one who will make [someone] a successor on the earth." *Khalīfa* (successor) is one who succeeds another. The meaning is "a successor from among you," because they (the jinn, or earlier inhabitants) were the inhabitants of the earth, and Adam and his descendants succeeded them in it.

If you ask: why was it not said *khalā'if* or *khulafā'* (plural forms)?

I answer: by *khalīfa* is meant Adam, and by mentioning him they dispensed with mentioning his offspring, just as the mention of the ancestor of a tribe is sufficient in your saying *Muḍar* and *Hāshim*. Or it may mean "one who will succeed you," or "a successor who will succeed you," and so it is singular for this reason. It was also read *khalīqa* with a *qāf*.

It is also possible that the meaning is "a successor of Mine," because Adam was God's successor on His earth, and so is every prophet: ﴿Indeed We have made you a successor on the earth﴾ (38:26).

If you ask: for what purpose did He inform them of this?

I answer: so that they would ask that question and be answered with what they were answered, and thus know the wisdom in their being made successors before their existence, as a safeguard for them against the objection of doubt at the time of their succession. It was also said: to teach His servants consultation in their affairs before undertaking them, and presenting them to their trustworthy and sincere advisers, although He, by His knowledge and perfect wisdom, is independent of consultation.

﴿They said: Will You place in it one who will spread corruption therein and shed blood...﴾ *Ataj'alu* is an expression of astonishment that people of disobedience should be made successors in place of people of obedience, while He is the Wise who does only good and wills only good.

[[The words "He is the Wise who does only good" and what follows are according to the Mu'tazilites. As for the People of the Sunna, He, exalted is He, does good and evil and wills both. (ʿ)]]

If you ask: how did they know this, so as to be astonished by it, when it is unseen?

I answer: they knew it by information from God, or from the Preserved Tablet (*al-lawḥ*), or it was established in their knowledge that the angels alone are the infallible creation, and that every creation other than them does not share their attribute. Or they analogized one of the two species (humans and jinn) to the other, since they settled the earth and corrupted it before the angels dwelt there.

It was read *yasfiku* with a *ḍamma* on the *fā'*, *yusfaku*, *yasfuk* (from *asfaka*), and *safaka*.

The *wāw* in *wa-naḥnu* (while we) is for the circumstantial state, as you say: "Do you do good to so-and-so while I have more right to it than him?"

*Al-tasbīḥ* (glorification) is declaring God far from evil, and likewise *taqdīs* (sanctification), from *sabaḥa* (to swim/travel) in the earth and water, and *qaddasa* in the earth: when one goes off in it and gets far away.

*Bi-ḥamdika* (with Your praise) is in the position of a circumstantial state: that is, "we glorify You while praising You and linked with Your praise," because were it not for Your favour upon us with success and gentleness, we would not be able to worship You.

﴿I know what you do not know﴾: that is, I know of the benefits in this matter what is hidden from you.

If you ask: why did He not explain those benefits to them?

I answer: it suffices the servants to know that all the acts of God are good and wise, even if the aspect of goodness and wisdom is hidden from them. Moreover, He did explain some of it in what follows: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾ (2:31). And the derivation of "Ādam" from *adama* (the brown colour/skin) and from *adīm al-arḍ* (the surface of the earth) is like their derivation of "Yaʿqūb" from *ʿaqab* (heel), "Idrīs" from *dars* (study), and "Iblīs" from *iblās* (despair). *Ādam* is a non-Arabic name, and the closest form of it is that it is on the pattern *fāʿal*, like *Āzar*, *ʿĀzar*, *ʿĀbir*, *Shālikh*, *Fāligh*, and similar names.

﴿The names, all of them﴾: that is, the names of the named things (*al-musammayāt*).

[[Mahmud, may God have mercy on him, said: "that is, the names of the named things, etc." Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: He flees from the belief that the name is the named, because that is the belief of the People of the Sunna, so he devises a stratagem to remove it from the implication of the verse by his words ﴿Inform them of their names﴾ (2:33), and he ignores His words ﴿Then He presented them to the angels﴾ (2:31). He also turns away from the wisdom of teaching, and that its connection is to the very words, with no great purpose in it. Rather, the important purpose is teaching him the essences of the named things, and making him acquainted with their realities and with the properties and secrets that God has placed in them, and with their names too. For the way of teaching distinguishes each reality by its name. So it is established by these two points that the meaning of "the names" is "the named things." As for his argument from His words ﴿Inform Me of the names of these﴾ (2:31), its best result is the addition of the names to the essences. They may say: if the names were the essences, it would entail the addition of a thing to itself; but that is not a valid objection, for this addition is like its counterpart in your saying "the self of Zayd and his reality." So the meaning is then "inform Me of the realities of these," and there is no objection to this addition, for the names are in the sense of the named things. The realities are more general than "these" that are pointed to and the one added to, so the addition is valid because of the difference between the more general and the more specific; and this is what validates the addition in "the self of Zayd" and similar expressions.

So this is a sample of the question of the name and the named, specific to this verse. In it, God willing, is sufficiency. Although the theologians count it among the science of *kalām*, it is overwhelmingly a verbal question, in which the disagreement between the Ash'arites and the Mu'tazilites does not return, in terms of reality, to much.]]

The genitive complement was omitted because it is known and indicated by the mention of "the names," since a name must have a named thing. In its place the definite article *al-* was given, as in His words ﴿and the head has blazed with grey﴾ (19:4).

If you ask: why not claim that the genitive was omitted and the complement put in its place, the original being "and He taught Adam the named things of the names"?

I answer: because teaching had to be connected to the names, not to the named things, by His words ﴿Inform Me of the names of these﴾ (2:31), and ﴿Inform them of their names﴾ and ﴿So when he informed them of their names﴾ (2:33). Just as the informing was connected to the names and not to the named things (He did not say "inform Me of these" or "inform them of them"), so the teaching had to be connected to them.

If you ask: what then is the meaning of His teaching him the names of the named things?

I answer: He showed him the kinds He had created, and taught him that this one's name is "horse," this one's name is "camel," this one's name is so-and-so, and this one's name is so-and-so; and He taught him their states and what is connected to them of religious and worldly benefits.

﴿Then He presented them﴾: that is, He presented the named things. He used the masculine pronoun because among the named things there are rational beings, so the masculine prevailed.

He asked them to inform Him, knowing their inability to inform, as a rebuke: ﴿if you are truthful﴾ (2:31), meaning in your claim that I will appoint as successors on the earth those who corrupt and shed blood, intending thereby to refute them, and that among those whom He appoints there are the scientific benefits which are the foundations of all benefits, for which they deserve to be appointed as successors. Thus He showed them that, and explained to them some of what had been left general of the benefits in their appointment, in His words ﴿I know what you do not know﴾ (2:30). His words ﴿Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth?﴾ (2:33) recall His words to them ﴿I know what you do not know﴾, except that He expressed it in a more expansive and clearer manner.

It was read *wa-ʿullima Ādam* with the passive. ʿAbdullah read *ʿaraḍahunna* (them, feminine plural), and Ubayy read *ʿaraḍahā* (it). The meaning is "He presented their named things" or "its named things," because presentation is not valid for names.

Abu Ja'far recited (lil-malā'ikati usjudū) with a ḍamma on the tā' by way of ittibāʿ (assimilation of the vowel). Raghadan is a description of the verbal noun: that is, eat abundantly, wide and pleasant. Ḥaythu is for an indefinite place, that is: in any place of Paradise you wish.

He permitted them to eat from Paradise in a far-reaching manner that removes any pretext, when He did not forbid them some of the food nor some of the places gathering the foods of Paradise, so that no excuse remains for them in partaking from one tree among its many trees, which are too numerous to count. It is said the tree was the wheat, or the vine, or the fig. It was also read (wa-lā tiqrabā) with a kasra on the tā'. Its precise sense: the Satan caused their slip to proceed from it. This "ʿan" is like its use in His saying: (And I did not do it of my own accord, ʿan amrī). And like the line:

(They forbid [people] from eating [a fat she-camel] and from drinking ...) describing a host who fed his guests to satiety; they walk and make a trace on the top of the mountain... The qunna (summit) of a mountain and its qulla is its highest point, while they are exceedingly fat, a fatness arising from much eating and much drinking.

It is said: (fa-azallahumā ʿan al-janna) means: He removed them from it and distanced them, as you say: zalla ʿan martabatihi (he slipped from his rank), and zalla ʿannī dhāka (that departed from me), and zalla min al-shahri kadhā (such-and-such departed from the month). It was also read: (fa-azālahumā). (Mimmā kānā fīhi): from the bliss and honour they were in.

Or [it means] "from Paradise," if the pronoun in (ʿanhā) refers to the tree. ʿAbdullāh read: (fa-waswasa lahumā al-shayṭān ʿanhā), and this is evidence that the pronoun refers to the tree, since the meaning is that his whispering proceeded from it. If you ask: how could he reach their slipping and whispering to them after it was said to him (fa-ukhruj minhā fa-innaka rajīm)? I say: it is permissible that entry into it be prevented in the manner of drawing near and honour, as the angels entered, while it is not prevented that he enter in the manner of whispering, as a trial for Adam and Eve.

It is said he used to draw near to the heaven and speak to them. It is said he stood at the gate and called out. It is reported that he wished to enter, but the guardians prevented him, so he entered into the mouth of the serpent until it entered with him while they were unaware. It is said (ihbiṭū) is addressed to Adam, Eve and Iblīs; and it is said [also to] the serpent. The correct view is that it is addressed to Adam and Eve, and what is meant is they and their offspring, since, as they were the origin of mankind and its branching-out, they were treated as if they were all of mankind. The proof for this is His saying: (He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others). This is further indicated by His saying: (Whoever follows My guidance, no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve; and those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those are the companions of the Fire, therein they will abide forever). And this is nothing but a ruling that encompasses all people. The meaning of (some of you enemies to others) is the mutual enmity and oppression that people have, and their misleading one another. Al-habūṭ: descent to the earth. (Mustaqarr): a place of settling, or settling; (wa-matāʿ): enjoyment and taking pleasure in life (ilā ḥīn): that is, until the Day of Resurrection. It is also said: until death.
