Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 2, verse 194:

The polytheists fought them in the year of al-Hudaybiyya, in the sacred month, which was Dhu al-Qa'da. It was said to them, when they set out for the making-up ('umra al-qada') and were averse to fighting, and that was in Dhu al-Qa'da: ﴿The sacred month for the sacred month﴾. That is, this month is (matched) with that month, and its violation with its violation, meaning: you violate its sanctity against them just as they violated its sanctity against you. ﴿And for sacred things there is retaliation﴾. That is, every sacred thing is subject to retaliation: whoever violates the sanctity of anything whatsoever, retaliation is taken from him by violating a sacred thing of his. So, since they violated the sanctity of your month, do the same to them and do not hesitate. He reinforced this with His saying: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you, and fear Allah﴾, while you are victorious over those who transgressed against you, so do not transgress beyond what is lawful for you.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 2, verse 195:

The bāʾ in ﴿بِأَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ is superfluous (zāʾidah), like it in "he gave with his hand to the one who submitted" (aʿṭā bi-yadihi lil-munqād). The meaning is: ﴿and do not cast yourselves into destruction with your hands﴾, that is, do not make them (your hands) grasp and hold you in their power. It was also said that ﴿with your hands﴾ means "with your selves," and it was said that its implied sense is: "do not throw yourselves with your hands," as one says: "So-and-so destroyed himself with his own hand," when he caused its ruin.

The meaning is a prohibition against abandoning spending in the way of God, since that is a cause of destruction; or against extravagance in spending, to the point of impoverishing oneself and neglecting one's dependants; or against recklessness and staking oneself (al-istiqtāl wal-ikhṭār bil-nafs); or against abandoning the military expedition (al-ghazw), which strengthens the enemy.

It is related that a man from the Emigrants (al-Muhājirūn) charged into the ranks of the enemy, and the people shouted at him: "He has cast his hand into destruction!" Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī said: "We know best about this verse; it was revealed concerning us. We accompanied the Messenger of God (ﷺ), supported him, witnessed the battles with him, and preferred him over our families, our wealth and our children. Then when Islam spread, its adherents multiplied, and the war laid down its burdens, we returned to our families, children and wealth, to repair them and settle among them. So the destruction was dwelling with family and wealth and abandoning jihad."[[Al-Tha'labi transmitted it through the chain of ʿUthmān al-Dārimī: he informed us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ, from al-Layth, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Aslam ibn ʿImrān — and he mentioned it in the same manner. Its original form is in Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī and al-Tirmidhī, from the narration of the aforementioned Aslam. He said: "We went out from Medina intending Constantinople, and over the body was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid ibn al-Walīd. A great host of the Romans came out of the city, and we arranged a great line of Muslims against them. A man from the Muslims charged into the Roman line until he entered among them. The people shouted: 'He has cast his hand into destruction!' Abū Ayyūb said: 'O people, [the hadith]...'" In al-Tirmidhī's narration it reads "and over the people was Faḍāla ibn ʿUbayd," and in al-Nasāʾī's narration "and over the people of Egypt was ʿUqba ibn Khālid," "and over the people of Syria was Faḍāla." Likewise it was transmitted by Aḥmad, Isḥāq, Abū Yaʿlā, al-Ṭabarī, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and others.]] Abū ʿAlī, in al-Ḥalabiyyāt, related from Abū ʿUbayda that al-tahlukah, al-halāk and al-halk are one and the same. He said: "This statement of Abū ʿUbayda indicates that al-tahlukah is a verbal noun (maṣdar)." A similar case is what Sībawayh related in the forms al-tuḍrah and al-tusrah and the like, and in nouns: al-tunḍibah and al-tunfulah. It is also permissible to say that its original form is al-tahlukah, like al-tajribah and al-tabṣirah and similar, being a verbal noun from halaka, and the kasrah was replaced by a ḍammah, as al-jiwār came in place of al-jiwār.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 2, verse 196:

﴿And complete the Hajj (pilgrimage) and the 'Umrah (lesser pilgrimage) for Allah.﴾ Perform them complete and whole, with their rites and conditions, for the sake of Allah's countenance, without any slackness or deficiency on your part in them. He said:

*"The completion of the Hajj is that the mounts halt*
*at a woman named Kharqa', her veil unlifted."*

[[By Dhu al-Rummah. Kharqa' is the name of his beloved from the Banu 'Amir. When he became infatuated with her, he ruined his riding gear and said: "The completion of our Hajj is that we visit Kharqa', and the mounts of a travelling man halt, so repair my gear for me." She said: "By Allah, I will not do the work well, for I am indeed kharqa', that is, foolish." The phrase "unveiling her face" is a circumstantial clause (hal) describing her, so that she is unveiling her face until he sees it. The addition of the description to its object is a verbal addition that does not confer definiteness, so it is valid as a circumstantial clause. It is related that one of the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-salih) said to his companion: "Has our Hajj been completed as Dhu al-Rummah said?" and he recited the verse.

It is said that its real intent is that, just as we have crossed the wastelands and reached His sanctuary, we should cut off the desires of the self until we witness the traces of His generosity. Thus his citing of the verse is by way of illustration (tamthil).]]

He made standing before her like one of the rites of the Hajj, without which it is not complete. It is said: its completion is that you enter the state of ihram for both from your household's dwelling-place. This is related from 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them. It is said: that you dedicate a separate journey to each of them, as Muhammad said: "A Hajj from Kufa and an 'Umrah from Kufa are better." It is said: that the expenditure be lawful. It is said: that you make both sincerely for worship and do not mix them with any trade or worldly aims.

If you ask: Is there evidence in it for the obligation of 'Umrah? I answer: It is merely a command to complete them, and there is no proof in that that they are obligatory or voluntary, for one may be commanded to complete both an obligatory act and a voluntary one. Unless you say: the command to complete them is a command to perform them, as evidenced by the reading of the one who read: ﴿And establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah﴾. The command is, in its origin, for obligation, unless some proof indicates otherwise, as it did in His saying ﴿then hunt﴾ and ﴿then disperse﴾ and the like. Then it is said to you: a proof has indicated the negation of obligation, namely what is related: it was said, "O Messenger of Allah, is 'Umrah obligatory like Hajj?" He said: "No, but to perform 'Umrah is better for you."

[[Related by al-Tirmidhi from the narration of Hajjaj ibn Arta'ah from Ibn al-Munkadir, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about 'Umrah: "Is it obligatory?" He said: "No. And to perform it is better." Al-Tabarani related it from the narration of 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir, with the wording "and to perform it is better for you." Al-Daraqutni related it through both routes and weakened it.]] And from him: "Hajj is struggle (jihad) and 'Umrah is voluntary."

Al-Tabarani related it from a hadith of Ibn 'Abbas similar to it, and in its chain is Muhammad ibn al-Fadl ibn 'Atiyyah, who is weak. Ibn Abi Dawud related it in al-Masahif through the narration of 'Umar ibn Qays from Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah from his paternal uncle from Mas'ud. Al-Daraqutni said in al-'Ilal: this is an error. Perhaps he meant Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talhah from his paternal uncle 'Abs ibn Talhah. This hadith is known only through the narration of Mu'awiyah ibn Ishaq ibn Talhah from his paternal aunt 'A'ishah bint Talhah from 'A'ishah. The memorizers among the companions of Shu'bah related it from Mu'awiyah ibn Ishaq from Abu Salih from Mahan as a mursal (broken chain). Likewise Ibn Abi Shaybah related it from Jarir from Mu'awiyah ibn Ishaq. Al-Bayhaqi said: it was related from Shu'bah with this chain connected, but the route to Shu'bah in it is weak.]]

If you say: It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Indeed, 'Umrah is the companion (qarinah) of Hajj." [[Related by al-Bukhari in suspended form (ta'liq), and by al-Shafi'i with a connected chain, through the narration of 'Amr ibn Dinar from Tawus from him.]] And from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man said to him: "I found Hajj and 'Umrah written upon me; I entered the state of ihram for both together." He said: "You have been guided to the sunnah of your Prophet." [[Related by Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and Ibn Hibban, from the narration of Abu Wa'il from al-Dabbi ibn Ma'bad.]] And since it is linked with Hajj in the command to complete, is it therefore obligatory like Hajj?

I answer: Its being a companion to Hajj means that the one who performs Qiran (combining both rites) combines them, and that they are mentioned together, so it is said: "So-and-so performed Hajj and 'Umrah," and "the pilgrims and the visitors (al-hajjaj wa al-'ummar)." Also because it is the lesser Hajj (al-hajj al-asghar). There is no proof in that for its being a companion to Hajj in obligation. As for the hadith of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, the man explained his statement that they were written upon him by his saying: "I entered ihram with them," and when one enters ihram for 'Umrah it becomes obligatory upon him, just as one who begins a voluntary prayer by takbir. The proof we mentioned excludes 'Umrah from the attribute of obligation, so Hajj alone remains obligatory. Thus they are like your saying: "Fast the month of Ramadan and six days of Shawwal," in that you command him with an obligation and a voluntary act.

'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and al-Sha'bi, may Allah be pleased with them, read ﴿and the 'Umrah for Allah﴾ with the nominative (raf'), as if they intended by that to remove it from the ruling of Hajj, which is obligation.

﴿But if you are prevented (uhsirtum)...﴾ It is said: "uhsira fulan" when a matter prevents him, such as fear, illness or incapacity. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿those who are restricted in the way of Allah﴾. And Ibn Mayyadah said:

*"Laylā's aversion was not that she had drifted far from you,*
*nor that a preoccupation had restrained you."*

[[By Tawbah ibn Humayyir, who says to himself: Laylā al-Akhyaliyyah's aversion toward you, your beloved, is not due to her distance from you, nor to preoccupations that held you back from her; rather, you abandoned her out of fear of watchers and slanderers. It is possible that the meaning is: her aversion toward you has no cause, and it is only to harm you and to burn your heart.]]

And "hussira" (was restricted) is when an enemy holds him back from proceeding, or imprisons him. From this comes the word "hasir" for one who is confined, and "al-hasir" for a king, because he is veiled (mahjub). This is the more common usage among them. Both mean prevention in every matter, like "sadda" and "asadda." Al-Farra' and Abu 'Amr al-Shaybani said likewise, and Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on them, held the same: any prevention, whether from an enemy, illness or otherwise, is valid in establishing the ruling of restriction (ihsar). According to Malik and al-Shafi'i, only prevention by an enemy counts.

And from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever is broken or lamed has been released (halla), and he must perform Hajj in the following year." [[Related by the authors of the Sunan, Ahmad, Ishaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah and al-Tabarani, from the hadith of 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Amr ibn Ghaziyyah al-Ansari.]]

﴿So what is feasible of the offering (fa-ma istaysara min al-hady)﴾: whatever is easy of it. It is said: "yassara al-amr" and "istaysara," as one says "sa'uba" and "asta'sba."

Hady is the plural of hadiyyah, as one says "jadi" for "jadiyyat al-sarj" (the padding of a saddle). [[His saying "jadiyyat al-sarj": in al-Sihah, "al-jadiyyah" with a sukun on the dal is a stuffed item placed beneath the two pommels of the saddle or the packsaddle. Then he said: likewise "al-jadiyyah" on the pattern fa'iliyyah. (Ghayn, i.e., the commentator's marker.)]] It is read ﴿min al-hadiyy﴾ with doubling, the plural of hadiyyah, like mutiyyah and mutiyy. The meaning is: if you are prevented from proceeding to the House while you are in ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah, then upon you, when you wish to exit the state of ihram, is what is feasible of the offering: a camel, a cow or a sheep. If you ask: Where and when is the offering of the one who is restricted slaughtered?

I answer: If he is a pilgrim (hajj), then at the Sanctuary (al-Haram), whenever he wishes, according to Abu Hanifah; he sends it, and he appoints for the one sent with it a day as a sign (amar). [[His saying "a day as a sign" (yawm amar): the wording of al-Baydawi is "yawm amarah"; when that day arrives and he thinks it has been slaughtered, he exits the state. In al-Sihah, al-Asma'i said: "al-amar" and "al-amarah" are the time and the sign. (Ghayn.)]] According to the two (Abu Yusuf and Muhammad), it is on the days of sacrifice (al-nahr). If he is an 'umrah performer, then at the Sanctuary at any time, according to all of them.

"What is feasible" is in the nominative as the subject, meaning: then upon him is what is feasible; or in the accusative: "then offer what is feasible."

﴿And do not shave your heads...﴾ The address is to those who are restricted: that is, do not exit the state until you know that the offering you have sent to the Sanctuary has reached its place (mahill), the place where it must be slaughtered. The "mahill" of the offering is the time of the obligation of its discharge, and this is clear according to the school of Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him.

If you ask: Did the Prophet (ﷺ) slaughter his offering where he was restricted?

[[As for the slaughter of the offering when he was restricted, it is in al-Bukhari from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he (ﷺ) went out performing 'Umrah, but the disbelievers of Quraysh prevented him from the House, so he slaughtered his offering and shaved his head at al-Hudaybiyyah. As for it being below Makkah, [blank in the original text] reported it.

As for the hadith of al-Zuhri, I have not found it, but al-Tabari related from the hadith of Najiyah ibn Jundub al-Aslami, who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) when he was barred from the House. I said: O Messenger of Allah, send with me the offering so that it may be slaughtered in the Sanctuary. He said: How will you do with it? I said: I will drive it through valleys where they cannot reach it. So I went off with it until I slaughtered it in the Sanctuary.]]

I say: The place of his restriction was the edge of al-Hudaybiyyah which lies toward the lower part of Makkah, and it is part of the Sanctuary. From al-Zuhri: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slaughtered his offering in the Sanctuary. Al-Waqidi said: al-Hudaybiyyah is the edge of the Sanctuary, nine miles from Makkah.

﴿But whoever among you is ill...﴾: whoever has an illness that necessitates shaving, ﴿or has an injury to his head﴾, which is lice or a wound, then upon him when he shaves is a ransom (fidyah): ﴿fasting three days, or giving charity to six needy persons, a half sa' of wheat for each needy person, or a sacrifice (nusuk)﴾, which is a sheep. It is related from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Perhaps your head has been troubling you, and lice?" He said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Shave your head and fast three days, or feed six needy persons, or sacrifice a sheep." [[Agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). It has a chain and wordings in the six books and elsewhere. The wording closest to the author's is what Malik related.]] Ka'b used to say:

"This verse was revealed concerning me." It is related that he passed by him while his head was sore, and he said: "This suffices as harm." [[Related by Ishaq in his Musnad, al-Tabarani and al-Daraqutni, from the narration of al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi from Abu Wa'il from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met me, and he wiped my head, and the lice scattered. He said: 'This suffices as harm. Go and shave and give charity to six needy persons.'" In the narration of Ishaq he said: "Indeed this is harm," and he commanded him to shave and to sacrifice, or to fast, or to feed.]] He commanded him to shave and to feed, or to fast. "Nusuk" is a verbal noun, and it is said it is the plural of nasikah. Al-Hasan read ﴿aw nusk﴾ with lightening.

﴿And when you are secure (amintum)...﴾ meaning: when you are not restricted and you are in safety and ease, ﴿then whoever performs tamattu' (enjoyment)﴾, that is, benefits by the 'Umrah ﴿until the Hajj﴾. His benefit by the 'Umrah until the time of Hajj is his drawing near to Allah the Exalted through it before drawing near through Hajj. It is also said: when he exits from his 'Umrah, he benefits by the permission of what had been forbidden to him until he enters ihram for Hajj.

﴿then what is feasible of the offering﴾: this is the offering of tamattu', and it is a rite (nusk) according to Abu Hanifah, and he eats from it. According to al-Shafi'i it falls under the category of penalties, and he does not eat from it. We slaughter it on the day of sacrifice, and according to him it is permissible to slaughter it once he has entered ihram for his Hajj.

﴿But whoever does not find (an offering), then a fast of three days during the Hajj﴾: during its time, which is its months, the period between the two ihrams, the ihram of 'Umrah and the ihram of Hajj. This is the school of Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him. It is best to fast on the day of Tarwiyah, the day of 'Arafah, and a day before them. If this time passes, only the blood offering suffices. According to al-Shafi'i, it may not be fasted except after entering ihram for Hajj, adhering to the apparent meaning of His saying ﴿during the Hajj﴾.

﴿And seven when you return (raja'tum)﴾: meaning when you depart and finish the acts of Hajj, according to Abu Hanifah. According to al-Shafi'i, it is returning to their families. Ibn Abi 'Ablah read ﴿wa sab'ah﴾ in the accusative, as a conjunction with the position (mahall) of "three days," as if it were said: "fasting three days," like His saying ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger an orphan﴾.

If you ask: What is the purpose of the summation (fadhlakah)?

I answer: The conjunction "and" may come to indicate permission, as in your saying: "Sit with al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin." Do you not see that if he sat with both of them, or with one of them, he would be complying? So the summation was made to negate the suspicion of permissibility.

Also, the purpose of the summation in every calculation is that the number is known as a whole just as it was known in detail, so that it may be comprehended, and from two directions, so that knowledge is confirmed. In the proverbs of the Arabs: "Two knowledges are better than one." Likewise ﴿kamilah﴾ (complete) is another emphasis. In it there is an added exhortation to fast it and not to neglect it or reduce its number, just as you say to a man when you have concern about a matter you command him and he is in a position to you: "Allah, Allah, do not fall short." It is also said: "kamilah" means it is complete in its occurrence as a substitute for the offering.

In the reading of Ubayy: ﴿fasting three days consecutively﴾.

﴿That (dhalika)﴾ refers to tamattu', according to Abu Hanifah and his companions. For them there is no tamattu' or qiran for the residents of the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram); whoever of them performs tamattu' or qiran owes a blood offering, which is a penalty (dam jinayah) of which he does not eat. As for the one who performs qiran and the one who performs tamattu' from the people of the distant regions (al-afaq), their blood offering is a rite (dam nusk), and they eat from it. According to al-Shafi'i, it refers to the ruling, namely the obligation of the offering or the fast, and he did not impose anything upon them. [[His saying "he did not impose anything upon them": that is, upon the residents of the Sacred Mosque. (Ghayn.)]] The residents of the Sacred Mosque are the people of the miqat stations and those within them up to Makkah, according to Abu Hanifah. According to al-Shafi'i, they are the people of the Sanctuary and those who are within the Sanctuary at a distance where prayer is not shortened.

﴿And fear Allah in guarding His limits and what He has commanded you and forbidden you in Hajj and otherwise. And know that Allah is severe in punishment﴾ upon whoever opposes Him, so that your knowledge of the severity of His punishment may be a kindness to you in piety.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 2, verse 197:

The time of the Hajj is "months" (ashhur), as when you say: "The cold is two months." The "known months" (al-ashhur al-ma'lumat) are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. [[Mahmud (al-Zamakhshari), may Allah have mercy on him, said: "They are Shawwal and Dhu al-Qa'dah... etc." Ahmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: What he (al-Zamakhshari) transmitted from Malik is one of his two opinions, and it is not the well-known view from him. As for his argument for this view by the disapproval of Umar of performing the 'umrah until the month of Muharram begins, it is not a proof for Malik, because he says: the 'umrah is not validly concluded during the days of Mina specifically for one who has performed the Hajj, until he completes the stoning (ramy) and becomes free (tahallul) by the ifadah (circumambulation), and then it is valid. The whole year other than what has been mentioned is a time (miqat) for 'umrah. The benefit of this opinion according to Malik does not appear except in dropping the sacrifice (dam) for delaying the tawaf al-ifadah until the end of Dhu al-Hijjah, and nothing else. This is the benefit which al-Zamakhshari transmitted from Urwah. By my life, this opinion is a good argument, and needs no further elaboration. But the apparent meaning of the verse and its implication is that the entire months are the time of the Hajj. Do you not see that whoever says "and ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah" needs, in order to make the verse fit his school, to establish that part of a month takes the place of all of it, and he cites as evidence his saying: "Thirty months in three states." He only needed to cite this because his statement departs from the apparent meaning of the verse. Whoever holds to it according to its apparent meaning, in the completeness of the three months, stands with its implication, without needing to add anything to it.]] According to Abu Hanifah. According to al-Shafi'i: the nine days of Dhu al-Hijjah and the night of the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr). According to Malik: all of Dhu al-Hijjah. If you ask: what is the benefit of limiting the Hajj to these months? I say: its benefit is that none of the acts of Hajj is valid except within them, and the ihram for Hajj is also not validly concluded outside them according to al-Shafi'i. According to Abu Hanifah it is validly concluded, but it is disliked. If you ask: how were two months and part of a third "months"? I say: the plural noun is shared by what is beyond the singular, as evidenced by the Almighty's saying: ﴿Your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ [66:4]. So there is no question in it. It would only be a point of question if it had been said: "three known months." It is also said: part of the month was given the status of its whole, as one says: "I saw you in such-and-such a year," or "in the time of so-and-so," while the period may be twenty years or more, and he saw him only in an hour of it. If you ask: what is the rationale for Malik's view, which is transmitted from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr? I say: they said that 'umrah is not recommended in these months according to Umar and Ibn Umar, so it is as if they are dedicated to Hajj, with no room for 'umrah in them. And from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he used to strike people with the whip and forbid them from performing 'umrah during them. And from Umar [[his saying "and from Umar" is perhaps Ibn Umar. (Gh.)]], may Allah be pleased with him, that he said to a man: "If you obey me, wait until, when the month of Muharram has begun [[his saying "until, when the month of Muharram has begun": in al-Sihah: "ahalla al-hilal" and "istahalla," in the passive form whose subject is not named. (Gh.)]], you go out to Dhat Irq and begin ihram from there with 'umrah." And they said: perhaps from the school of Urwah is the permissibility of delaying the tawaf al-ziyarah until the end of the month. [...] Known and recognized by people, they will not be confused about them. And in it: the Shari'ah did not come contrary to what they knew; rather it came confirming it. "Whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj in them": whoever obligates himself to it by talbiyah or by garlanding the sacrificial animal and driving it, according to Abu Hanifah, and according to al-Shafi'i by intention. ﴿There shall be no obscenity (rafath)﴾: by consensus, because it invalidates it. Or: no vulgarity of speech. ﴿Nor wickedness (fusuq)﴾: nor going beyond the bounds of the Shari'ah. It is also said: it is abuse and calling one another by offensive nicknames. ﴿Nor disputing (jidal)﴾: nor quarrelling with companions, servants, and muleteers [[his saying "and the muleteers": in al-Sihah: al-kira' is with a long vowel, being a verbal noun of kariitu. The proof of that is that you say: a man who is a muleteer (makkar). And mufa'il is from fa'alta. So "al-makkarin" in the words of the commentator is the plural of al-mukari, on the pattern of al-mufa'ilin as the plural of al-mufa'il. (Gh.)]]. He was only commanded to avoid that, and it is obligatory to avoid it in every situation [[Mahmud, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "He was only commanded to avoid that in the Hajj, and avoiding it is obligatory... etc." Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: In it is a subtle point related to the science of rhetoric: specifying the Hajj with the prohibition of obscenity, wickedness, and disputing in it indicates that these are in other than the Hajj, although they are forbidden and ugly; however, that ugliness established for them outside the Hajj is as nothing compared with their occurrence within the Hajj. So this specification includes this kind of eloquent exaggeration, and Allah knows best. Moreover, if rafath means only speaking about matters of intercourse, then the prohibition of it is specific to the Hajj, and it is permitted outside it in the lawful manner. Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, pointed out that there is no harm for the pilgrim in dealing with matters concerning women, but this may cause the misconception that it leads to neglecting what is forbidden; and this indicates Malik's strictness in forbidding obscenity for the pilgrim and what relates to it, and Allah knows best. I have heard the Shafi'is persistently object to Ishaq in his statement in al-Tanbih: "and the prohibition of backbiting for the fasting person." They say: "And for the one who breaks the fast," so there is no benefit in specifying the fasting person; and they count that as an error from him. They are far from this verse and its like. I have given him a wide excuse for that phrasing, since the Glorious Book is the test of eloquence and soundness of expression.]] because with the Hajj it is more repugnant, like wearing silk in prayer and melodious chanting in the recitation of the Qur'an. The intent of the negation is the obligation of their absence, and that they are by nature such that they should not exist. The three negated terms are read in the accusative and in the nominative. Abu 'Amr and Ibn Kathir read the first two in the nominative and the last in the accusative, because they understood the first two in the sense of a prohibition, as if it were said: "let there be no obscenity or wickedness," and the third in the sense of informing of the absence of disputing, as if it were said: "there is no doubt and no dispute in the Hajj." That is because the Quraysh differed from all the other Arabs: they stood at al-Mash'ar al-Haram, while all the other Arabs stood at 'Arafah. They used to advance the Hajj one year and delay it another year, which is the nasi'; so it was returned to one fixed time, and the standing was returned to 'Arafah. Thus Allah the Exalted informed that the disagreement concerning the Hajj had been removed. He used as evidence that what is forbidden is obscenity and wickedness, not disputing, the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Whoever performs Hajj and does not commit obscenity or wickedness returns like the day his mother bore him." [Agreed upon, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.] And he did not mention disputing. ﴿Whatever good you do, Allah knows it﴾: an exhortation to good following the prohibition of evil, and that they should employ good speech in place of foul speech, righteousness and piety in place of wickedness, and agreement and good character in place of disputing. Or the doing of good is made an expression for restraining themselves so that nothing forbidden to them is found in them, and the saying of the Exalted supports this: ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is piety (taqwa)﴾ [2:197], meaning: make your provision for the Hereafter the avoidance of ugly deeds, for the best provision is their avoidance. It is also said: the people of Yemen used not to take provisions and would say: "We rely upon Allah, and we perform Hajj to the House of Allah; will He not feed us?" so they would become a burden upon people. So it was revealed concerning them. Its meaning: take provision and fear begging and imposing upon people and burdening them, for the best provision is piety. ﴿And fear Me﴾: and dread My punishment. ﴿O people of understanding (ulu al-albab)﴾: meaning that the requirement of intellect is the fear of Allah, and whoever among the intelligent does not fear Him is as if he had no intellect.

فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ ﴿fadlan min rabbikum﴾: an enrichment and a gift from Him, and it means profit and gain through trade. Some of the Arabs considered it sinful to trade during the days of the Hajj. When the ten days began, they refrained from buying and selling, so no market was held for them. They called anyone who went out to trade al-Dāj, and they would say: "These are the dāj, and they are not the ḥājj (pilgrims)." It was said that ʿUkāz, Majannah and Dhū al-Majāz were their markets in the Jahiliyyah, where they traded during the season, and their livelihood came from them. When Islam came, they regarded it as sinful, so Allah lifted the blame from them in this matter and permitted it for them. Trade is permitted only so long as it does not distract from worship.

It is related from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man said to him: "We are a people who hire out our camels on this route, and some people claim that we have no Hajj." He said: "A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about what you have asked, and he did not answer him, until ﴿There is no blame upon you﴾ was revealed. Then he called for him and said: 'You are pilgrims.'" [[Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Shaybah and al-Ḥākim narrated it through al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Musayyib: Abū Umāmah al-Taymī narrated to us, who said: "I used to hire out (my camel) on this route, and a people would say: 'You have no Hajj.' So I met Ibn ʿUmar, and he said: 'Are you not in the state of iḥrām? But—' the hadith..."]]

It is also related from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was asked: "Did you used to dislike trade during the Hajj?" He said: "Was our livelihood anything but trade during the Hajj?" [[al-Ṭabarī narrated it through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muhājir from Abū Ṣāliḥ, the client of ʿUmar, who said: "I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful...' and he mentioned it." In its chain is Mandal ibn ʿAlī, who is weak.]]

Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, recited: ﴿fadlan min rabbikum fī mawāsim al-ḥajj﴾ (a gift from your Lord during the seasons of the Hajj). ﴿in tabtaghū﴾ (in that you seek) ﴿an tabtaghū﴾ [[The words "an tabtaghū" should have been placed before the explanation of His words, ﴿fadlan min rabbikum﴾. (ʿ)]] ﴿afaḍtum﴾: you pressed on in large numbers (dafaʿtum bi-kathrah). It is from the pouring of water, which is pouring abundantly. Its original form was afaḍtum anfusakum (you poured yourselves forth), and the object was omitted, as it is omitted in dafaʿū min mawḍiʿ kadhā (they pushed from such-and-such a place) and ṣabbū (they poured).

In the hadith of Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him [[I have not found it. What is in al-Gharāʾib by Abū ʿUbayd al-Jurmī. In Musnad al-Shāfiʿī and Ṭabaqāt Ibn Saʿd, all from the hadith of Ibn ʿUyaynah from Ibn al-Munkadir, and from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿīd ibn Yarbūʿ from Jubayr ibn al-Ḥuwayrith who said: "I saw Abū Bakr on Qaza', and he was urging his camel with his staff." Al-Jurmī added from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah from Ibn ʿUyaynah: "As if I were looking at his thigh, and it had become uncovered."]]: "He poured forth (ṣabba) at Dafrān, and he was urging (yakhrush) his camel with his staff." [[In some copies it is "Dhafrān," with the letter dhāl and fāʾ. Perhaps the first is with dāl and fāʾ, from al-dafar meaning stench only. Al-dhafar, with dhāl and fāʾ and a vowel, means the sharpness of a smell, whether pleasant or foul, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. As for al-daqar with dāl and qāf, it means harshness, lying, obscenity and slander. This is from al-Ṣiḥāḥ, and in it: al-khirsh is like al-khadsh. (ʿ)]]

They say: "They plunged into the talk (afāḍū fī al-ḥadīth) and burst out with it (ḥaḍabū fīhi)." [[In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: al-haḍbah is a downpour, and haḍaba al-qawm and ihtaḍabū fī al-ḥadīth means they poured into it. (ʿ)]]

﴿ʿArafāt﴾ is a name for the place of standing, named with a plural form like Adhruʿāt. If you say: "Why is it not made diptote (ghayr munṣarif), when it has two causes (of diptotic inflection): the definite form and the feminine?" I say: It cannot be free of the feminine. Either it is with the tāʾ that is in its wording, or with an implied tāʾ, as in Suʿād. The tāʾ in its wording is not a feminine marker. Rather, it is, together with the alif before it, the sign of the feminine plural. The tāʾ cannot be implied in it, because this tāʾ, by being specific to the feminine plural, prevents its being implied, just as the tāʾ of the feminine cannot be implied in bint (daughter), since the tāʾ which replaces the wāw, by being specific to the feminine like the tāʾ of the feminine, refuses to be implied.

They said: It was named so because it was described to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and when he saw it, he recognized it (ʿarafahā). It was said that when Jibrīl was taking him around the holy places, he showed it to him and said: "You have recognized it (qad ʿarafta)." It was said: Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ met there and recognized one another (taʿārafā). It was said: Because people recognize one another there. Allah knows the reality of that best. It is one of the names that were coined (murtajalah), because ʿarafah is not known among the names of kinds, except to be the plural of ʿārif (one who knows).

It was said: In it there is evidence that standing at ʿArafah is obligatory, because the outpouring (ifāḍah) cannot occur except after it. It is related from the Prophet ﷺ: "Hajj is ʿArafah; whoever attains ʿArafah has attained the Hajj." [[Narrated by the compilers of the Sunan and al-Ḥākim, and the wording is from al-Nasāʾī, who added: "before the dawn rises." All of them from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yaʿmar al-Dīlī, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

﴿fa-dhkurū Allāh﴾ (so remember Allah): with the talbiyah, the tahlīl, the takbīr, praise and supplications. It was said: with the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers. ﴿al-mash ʿar al-ḥarām﴾ is Quzaḥ, the mountain on which the Imam stands, and on which there is a fire-beacon (al-mīqadah). It was said: the Mashʿar al-Ḥarām is what lies between the mountain of Muzdalifah, from the two narrow passes of ʿArafah [[His words "from the two narrow passes of ʿArafah": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, al-maʾzam is the narrow passage, and also the place of battle. (ʿ)]] to the valley of Muḥassir. Neither the two passes nor the valley of Muḥassir is part of the Mashʿar al-Ḥarām. The correct view is that it is the mountain, because of what Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, related: that when the Prophet ﷺ prayed the dawn prayer at Muzdalifah in the darkness, he mounted his she-camel and came to the Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, and he supplicated, glorified (kabbara) and declared the unity of Allah (hallala), and he remained standing until it became light. [[Narrated by Muslim in the chapter on the description of the Hajj, in the long hadith.]]

His words ﴿ʿinda al-mash ʿar al-ḥarām﴾ mean: in the direction of the Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, near to it, for the sake of its merit, like being near the Mountain of Mercy. Otherwise, all of Muzdalifah is a place of standing except the valley of Muḥassir. Or the ʿaqāb (rear parts) of Muzdalifah were made to be the Mashʿar, since they have the ruling of the Mashʿar and are joined to it, near the Mashʿar. The mashʿar means the sign, because it is the sign of worship.

It is described as al-ḥarām because of its sanctity. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him, that he looked at the people on the night of Jamʿ and said: "I have seen people this night who do not sleep." It was said: Muzdalifah was called Jamʿ because Ādam, peace be upon him, gathered there with Ḥawwāʾ, and he drew near to her (izdalafa ilayhā), meaning he approached her. It is related from Qatādah: because the two prayers are combined there (yujmaʿu). It is permissible to say: it is described by the act of its people, because they draw near (yazdalifūn) to Allah, that is, they seek nearness by standing there.

﴿kamā hadākum﴾: here mā is either a verbal-source particle (maṣdariyyah) or a preventive particle (kāffah). The meaning: remember Him with a good remembrance, as He guided you with good guidance; and remember Him as He taught you how to remember Him, and do not deviate from it. ﴿wa-in kuntum min qablihi﴾ (though before it you were): before the guidance, ﴿la-mina al-ḍāllīn﴾ (certainly among those who were astray), the ignorant, who did not know how to remember Him and worship Him. Here in is the lightened form of the heavy in (inna), and the lām is the distinguishing lām.

﴿thumma afīḍū﴾ (then pour forth): then let your outpouring be ﴿min ḥaythu afāḍa al-nās﴾ (from where the people poured forth), and do not be from Muzdalifah. This is because of what the Ḥums (Quraysh and their allies) were upon of arrogance over the people and haughtiness over them, and their exalting themselves above standing with the others. And their saying: "We are the people of Allah and the dwellers of His sanctuary, so we will not leave it," and so they stand at Jamʿ while all other people stand at ʿArafāt. [[Maḥmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: "Al-Zamakhsharī, may Allah have mercy on him: 'That is because of what the Ḥums were upon of arrogance over the people...' (etc.)." Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The verse includes two points. First: the coordination of the two outpourings, one upon the other, with a single referent, which is the outpouring commanded. Someone might suppose it is coordination of a thing with itself, and this supposition is removed by the fact that between them there is the difference that exists between the general and the specific: the first statement is the outpouring in its unrestricted form, and the second command is the outpouring restricted by equality with the people. Second: after clarifying the soundness of the coordination, its being introduced by the particle thumma (then), which implies delay in addition to difference, while there is no delay between the absolute and the restricted addition. The answer: delay may be in terms of time, and it may also be in terms of the elevation of rank and the distance in height relative to others, and this is what he answered with after further vigor and clarification.]]

Then you asked: "What is the position of thumma?" I say: Its position is like its position in your saying: "Be kind to people, then do not be kind to other than the noble," where you use thumma to indicate the difference between being kind to the noble and being kind to others, and the distance between them. Likewise, when He commanded them to remember Him at the outpouring from ʿArafāt, He said: "Then pour forth," to show the difference between the two outpourings, and that one of them is correct and the other is mistaken.

It was said: "Then pour forth from where the people poured forth" means the Ḥums, that is, from Muzdalifah to Minā after the outpouring from ʿArafāt. It was read: "min ḥaythu afāḍa al-nāsī" with a kasrah on the sīn, that is, al-nāsī, who is Ādam, from His words: ﴿And We had already made a covenant with Ādam before, but he forgot (fa-nasiya)﴾. It means that the outpouring from ʿArafāt is an ancient law, so do not oppose it.

﴿wa-istaghfirū Allāh﴾ (and ask Allah for forgiveness): for your opposition in the standing place and similar matters of your ignorance. ﴿fa-idhā qaḍaytum manāsikakum﴾ (so when you have completed your rites): that is, when you have finished your acts of worship of Hajj and have departed. ﴿fa-dhkurū Allāh kadhikrikum ābāʾakum﴾ (then remember Allah as you remember your fathers): so increase the remembrance of Allah and go to extremes in it, as you do in remembering your fathers, their glories and their days. When they had completed their rites, they would stand between the mosque at Minā and the mountain, enumerating the virtues of their fathers and mentioning the good qualities of their days.

﴿aw ashadda dhikran﴾ (or with a greater remembrance): in a position of genitive (jarr) by coordination with what the remembrance is attached to in His words ﴿kadhikrikum﴾, as you say: "like the remembrance of Quraysh of their fathers, or of a people greater than them in remembrance." Or in an accusative position by coordination with ābāʾakum, meaning: or more intense in remembrance than your fathers, on the basis that dhikran is the tamyīz (specification) of the one who remembers. [[Mahmūd, may Allah have mercy on him: "Ashadd is coordinated with what the remembrance is attached to..." Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him: On the first view, ashadd refers to the thing remembered as the object. An example of the first: two people strike Zayd as an example, and one asks: "Which of them is more intense in striking Zayd?" and he refers it to the striker. An example of the second: Zayd strikes two people as an example, and you say: "Which of them is more intense in striking?" and you refer it to the one struck. On the first view, the preference is for the agent, which is the analogical form. On the second, the preference is for the object, which is contrary to analogy. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned in his Mufaṣṣal that it is irregular, with their saying: "Atasabbalu mirʾat al-taḥsīn wa-anā asarru minka" (in these examples he enumerated). I wonder how he applied the verse to it, when another path was available. In both views there is an escape from coordinating ashadd with the first remembrance, lest it refer to the remembrance while the remembrance has been put in the accusative as a tamyīz from it, so the remembrance would be remembering itself, which is impossible. But Abū al-Fatḥ (Ibn Jinnī) corrected this view and linked it to the pattern of their saying: "shaʿara shāʿir" and "janna junūnuh," and similar expressions in which the Arabs went to extremes, making an attribute have an attribute like itself, to establish its existence. It is clarified that the accusative of the remembrance as tamyīz requires that ashadd not refer to it, and determines that it is excluded from it, either by its referring to the remembering body by interpreting it as making it a remembering agent, as Abū al-Fatḥ arrived at: if you say "Zayd akram abā," then Zayd would be among the sons; and if you say "Zayd akram ab," he would be among the fathers. It is possible to coordinate it with the remembrance, meaning another way besides what Abū al-Fatḥ went to, namely the matter Sībawayh mentioned: "They say: 'He is ashaḥḥ al-nās rajulan (most miserly of people in a man), and hum khayr al-nās rajulan (they are the best of people in a man), and hum khayr al-nās ithnayn (they are the best of people in two).'" Here the genitive is in the position of the tanwīn, and rajul and ithnayn are accusative, just as wajh is accusative in your saying "huwa aḥsanu minhu wajhan." It is not except indefinite, just as the ḥāl (circumstantial) is not except indefinite. The rajul is the subject of the beginning. He meant by this that this is not like "huwa ashjaʿu al-nās ghulāman," for this may be that ghulām is the subject of the beginning, as in the first example, and it may be other than it. The verse in this way that I have clarified is placed on the first example, so the accusative mention refers to ashadd just as rajul (in the accusative) referred to ashaḥḥ. It is as if he said: "or the most intense of remembrances in remembrance." These are four ways, all of which have been trodden, except this way which I added, for my reflection has made that clear. ﴿ka-khashyati Allāh aw ashadda khashyah﴾ (like the fear of Allah or more intense fear). I did not come across al-Zamakhsharī's words on it after that.]]

﴿fa-minā al-nās man yaqūlu﴾ (among people is he who says): its meaning is: increase the remembrance and supplication of Allah, for people are divided between one who seeks through the remembrance of Allah nothing but the goods of this world, and one who seeks the good of both abodes. So be among the ones who increase. ﴿rabbanā ātinā fī al-dunyā﴾ (Our Lord, give us in this world): make our giving, that is, our provision, in this world only. ﴿wa-mā lahu fī al-ākhirati min khalāq﴾ (and he has no portion in the Hereafter): that is, whoever seeks my portion (khalāqī), which is share. Or: this caller has no share in the Hereafter, because his concern is limited to this world.

The two good things (al-ḥasanatān) are what the righteous seek in this world: health, sufficiency, and success in good; and what they seek in the Hereafter: reward. It is related from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him: "The good in this world is a righteous wife, and in the Hereafter the maiden of paradise (ḥawrāʾ). The punishment of the Fire is an evil wife." ﴿ulāʾika al-dāʿūna bi-al-ḥasanatayni lahum naṣībun mimmā kasabū﴾ (those are the ones who ask for the two good things; for them is a share of what they earned): that is, a share of the same kind as what they earned of good deeds, which is the reward, the good benefits. Or: from the sake of what they earned, as in His words: ﴿mimmā khaṭīʾātihim ughriqū﴾ (because of their sins they were drowned). Or: they have a share of what they asked for, and We will give them what they deserve according to their interests in this world and their merit in the Hereafter. Supplication was called earning because it is one of the deeds, and deeds are described as earned: ﴿bimā kasabat aydīkum﴾ (by what your hands have earned). It is permissible that ﴿ulāʾika﴾ refers to both groups together, and that each group has a share of the kind of what they earned.

﴿wa-Allāhu sarīʿu al-ḥisāb﴾ (and Allah is swift in reckoning): He is about to establish the Resurrection and call the servants to account. So hasten to increase the remembrance and to seek the Hereafter. Or: He described Himself as swift in reckoning the creatures despite their great number and the abundance of their deeds, to show the perfection of His power and the necessity of being wary of Him.

It is related that He reckons all creation in the time it takes to milk a sheep. It is related: in the time between two milkings of a she-camel. It is related: in the time of a single blink.

فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ ﴿fadlan min rabbikum﴾: an enrichment and a gift from Him, and it means profit and gain through trade. Some of the Arabs considered it sinful to trade during the days of the Hajj. When the ten days began, they refrained from buying and selling, so no market was held for them. They called anyone who went out to trade al-Dāj, and they would say: "These are the dāj, and they are not the ḥājj (pilgrims)." It was said that ʿUkāz, Majannah and Dhū al-Majāz were their markets in the Jahiliyyah, where they traded during the season, and their livelihood came from them. When Islam came, they regarded it as sinful, so Allah lifted the blame from them in this matter and permitted it for them. Trade is permitted only so long as it does not distract from worship.

It is related from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man said to him: "We are a people who hire out our camels on this route, and some people claim that we have no Hajj." He said: "A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about what you have asked, and he did not answer him, until ﴿There is no blame upon you﴾ was revealed. Then he called for him and said: 'You are pilgrims.'" [[Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Shaybah and al-Ḥākim narrated it through al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Musayyib: Abū Umāmah al-Taymī narrated to us, who said: "I used to hire out (my camel) on this route, and a people would say: 'You have no Hajj.' So I met Ibn ʿUmar, and he said: 'Are you not in the state of iḥrām? But—' the hadith..."]]

It is also related from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was asked: "Did you used to dislike trade during the Hajj?" He said: "Was our livelihood anything but trade during the Hajj?" [[al-Ṭabarī narrated it through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muhājir from Abū Ṣāliḥ, the client of ʿUmar, who said: "I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful...' and he mentioned it." In its chain is Mandal ibn ʿAlī, who is weak.]]

Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, recited: ﴿fadlan min rabbikum fī mawāsim al-ḥajj﴾ (a gift from your Lord during the seasons of the Hajj). ﴿in tabtaghū﴾ (in that you seek) ﴿an tabtaghū﴾ [[The words "an tabtaghū" should have been placed before the explanation of His words, ﴿fadlan min rabbikum﴾. (ʿ)]] ﴿afaḍtum﴾: you pressed on in large numbers (dafaʿtum bi-kathrah). It is from the pouring of water, which is pouring abundantly. Its original form was afaḍtum anfusakum (you poured yourselves forth), and the object was omitted, as it is omitted in dafaʿū min mawḍiʿ kadhā (they pushed from such-and-such a place) and ṣabbū (they poured).

In the hadith of Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him [[I have not found it. What is in al-Gharāʾib by Abū ʿUbayd al-Jurmī. In Musnad al-Shāfiʿī and Ṭabaqāt Ibn Saʿd, all from the hadith of Ibn ʿUyaynah from Ibn al-Munkadir, and from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿīd ibn Yarbūʿ from Jubayr ibn al-Ḥuwayrith who said: "I saw Abū Bakr on Qaza', and he was urging his camel with his staff." Al-Jurmī added from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah from Ibn ʿUyaynah: "As if I were looking at his thigh, and it had become uncovered."]]: "He poured forth (ṣabba) at Dafrān, and he was urging (yakhrush) his camel with his staff." [[In some copies it is "Dhafrān," with the letter dhāl and fāʾ. Perhaps the first is with dāl and fāʾ, from al-dafar meaning stench only. Al-dhafar, with dhāl and fāʾ and a vowel, means the sharpness of a smell, whether pleasant or foul, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. As for al-daqar with dāl and qāf, it means harshness, lying, obscenity and slander. This is from al-Ṣiḥāḥ, and in it: al-khirsh is like al-khadsh. (ʿ)]]

They say: "They plunged into the talk (afāḍū fī al-ḥadīth) and burst out with it (ḥaḍabū fīhi)." [[In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: al-haḍbah is a downpour, and haḍaba al-qawm and ihtaḍabū fī al-ḥadīth means they poured into it. (ʿ)]]

Then you asked: "What is the position of thumma?" I say: Its position is like its position in your saying: "Be kind to people, then do not be kind to other than the noble," where you use thumma to indicate the difference between being kind to the noble and being kind to others, and the distance between them. Likewise, when He commanded them to remember Him at the outpouring from ʿArafāt, He said: "Then pour forth," to show the difference between the two outpourings, and that one of them is correct and the other is mistaken.

It was read: "min ḥaythu afāḍa al-nāsī" with a kasrah on the sīn, that is, al-nāsī, who is Ādam, from His words: ﴿And We had already made a covenant with Ādam before, but he forgot (fa-nasiya)﴾. ﴿wa-istaghfirū Allāh﴾ (and ask Allah for forgiveness): for your opposition in the standing place and similar matters of your ignorance. ﴿fa-idhā qaḍaytum manāsikakum﴾ (so when you have completed your rites): that is, when you have finished your acts of worship of Hajj and have departed. ﴿fa-dhkurū Allāh kadhikrikum ābāʾakum﴾ (then remember Allah as you remember your fathers): so increase the remembrance of Allah and go to extremes in it, as you do in remembering your fathers, their glories and their days. When they had completed their rites, they would stand between the mosque at Minā and the mountain, enumerating the virtues of their fathers and mentioning the good qualities of their days.

﴿aw ashadda dhikran﴾ (or with a greater remembrance): in a position of genitive (jarr) by coordination with what the remembrance is attached to in His words ﴿kadhikrikum﴾, as you say: "like the remembrance of Quraysh of their fathers, or of a people greater than them in remembrance." Or in an accusative position by coordination with ābāʾakum, meaning: or more intense in remembrance than your fathers, on the basis that dhikran is the tamyīz (specification) of the one who remembers. [[Mahmūd, may Allah have mercy on him: "Ashadd is coordinated with what the remembrance is attached to..." Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him: On the first view, ashadd refers to the thing remembered as the object. An example of the first: two people strike Zayd as an example, and one asks: "Which of them is more intense in striking Zayd?" and he refers it to the striker. An example of the second: Zayd strikes two people as an example, and you say: "Which of them is more intense in striking?" and you refer it to the one struck. On the first view, the preference is for the agent, which is the analogical form. On the second, the preference is for the object, which is contrary to analogy. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned in his Mufaṣṣal that it is irregular, with their saying: "Atasabbalu mirʾat al-taḥsīn wa-anā asarru minka" (in these examples he enumerated). I wonder how he applied the verse to it, when another path was available. In both views there is an escape from coordinating ashadd with the first remembrance, lest it refer to the remembrance while the remembrance has been put in the accusative as a tamyīz from it, so the remembrance would be remembering itself, which is impossible. But Abū al-Fatḥ (Ibn Jinnī) corrected this view and linked it to the pattern of their saying: "shaʿara shāʿir" and "janna junūnuh," and similar expressions in which the Arabs went to extremes, making an attribute have an attribute like itself, to establish its existence. It is clarified that the accusative of the remembrance as tamyīz requires that ashadd not refer to it, and determines that it is excluded from it, either by its referring to the remembering body by interpreting it as making it a remembering agent, as Abū al-Fatḥ arrived at: if you say "Zayd akram abā," then Zayd would be among the sons; and if you say "Zayd akram ab," he would be among the fathers. It is possible to coordinate it with the remembrance, meaning another way besides what Abū al-Fatḥ went to, namely the matter Sībawayh mentioned: "They say: 'He is ashaḥḥ al-nās rajulan (most miserly of people in a man), and hum khayr al-nās rajulan (they are the best of people in a man), and hum khayr al-nās ithnayn (they are the best of people in two).'" Here the genitive is in the position of the tanwīn, and rajul and ithnayn are accusative, just as wajh is accusative in your saying "huwa aḥsanu minhu wajhan." It is not except indefinite, just as the ḥāl (circumstantial) is not except indefinite. The rajul is the subject of the beginning. He meant by this that this is not like "huwa ashjaʿu al-nās ghulāman," for this may be that ghulām is the subject of the beginning, as in the first example, and it may be other than it. The verse in this way that I have clarified is placed on the first example, so the accusative mention refers to ashadd just as rajul (in the accusative) referred to ashaḥḥ. It is as if he said: "or the most intense of remembrances in remembrance." These are four ways, all of which have been trodden, except this way which I added, for my reflection has made that clear. ﴿ka-khashyati Allāh aw ashadda khashyah﴾ (like the fear of Allah or more intense fear). I did not come across al-Zamakhsharī's words on it after that.]]

﴿fa-minā al-nās man yaqūlu﴾ (among people is he who says): its meaning is: increase the remembrance and supplication of Allah, for people are divided between one who seeks through the remembrance of Allah nothing but the goods of this world, and one who seeks the good of both abodes. So be among the ones who increase. ﴿rabbanā ātinā fī al-dunyā﴾ (Our Lord, give us in this world): make our giving, that is, our provision, in this world only. ﴿wa-mā lahu fī al-ākhirati min khalāq﴾ (and he has no portion in the Hereafter): that is, whoever seeks my portion (khalāqī), which is share. Or: this caller has no share in the Hereafter, because his concern is limited to this world.

The two good things (al-ḥasanatān) are what the righteous seek in this world: health, sufficiency, and success in good; and what they seek in the Hereafter: reward. It is related from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him: "The good in this world is a righteous wife, and in the Hereafter the maiden of paradise (ḥawrāʾ). The punishment of the Fire is an evil wife." ﴿ulāʾika al-dāʿūna bi-al-ḥasanatayni lahum naṣībun mimmā kasabū﴾ (those are the ones who ask for the two good things; for them is a share of what they earned): that is, a share of the same kind as what they earned of good deeds, which is the reward, the good benefits. Or: from the sake of what they earned, as in His words: ﴿mimmā khaṭīʾātihim ughriqū﴾ (because of their sins they were drowned). Or: they have a share of what they asked for, and We will give them what they deserve according to their interests in this world and their merit in the Hereafter. Supplication was called earning because it is one of the deeds, and deeds are described as earned: ﴿bimā kasabat aydīkum﴾ (by what your hands have earned). It is permissible that ﴿ulāʾika﴾ refers to both groups together, and that each group has a share of the kind of what they earned.

﴿wa-Allāhu sarīʿu al-ḥisāb﴾ (and Allah is swift in reckoning): He is about to establish the Resurrection and call the servants to account. So hasten to increase the remembrance and to seek the Hereafter. Or: He described Himself as swift in reckoning the creatures despite their great number and the abundance of their deeds, to show the perfection of His power and the necessity of being wary of Him.

It is related that He reckons all creation in the time it takes to milk a sheep. It is related: in the time between two milkings of a she-camel. It is related: in the time of a single blink.

فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ ﴿fadlan min rabbikum﴾: an enrichment and a gift from Him, and it means profit and gain through trade. Some of the Arabs considered it sinful to trade during the days of the Hajj. When the ten days began, they refrained from buying and selling, so no market was held for them. They called anyone who went out to trade al-Dāj, and they would say: "These are the dāj, and they are not the ḥājj (pilgrims)." It was said that ʿUkāz, Majannah and Dhū al-Majāz were their markets in the Jahiliyyah, where they traded during the season, and their livelihood came from them. When Islam came, they regarded it as sinful, so Allah lifted the blame from them in this matter and permitted it for them. Trade is permitted only so long as it does not distract from worship.

It is related from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man said to him: "We are a people who hire out our camels on this route, and some people claim that we have no Hajj." He said: "A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about what you have asked, and he did not answer him, until ﴿There is no blame upon you﴾ was revealed. Then he called for him and said: 'You are pilgrims.'" [[Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Shaybah and al-Ḥākim narrated it through al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Musayyib: Abū Umāmah al-Taymī narrated to us, who said: "I used to hire out (my camel) on this route, and a people would say: 'You have no Hajj.' So I met Ibn ʿUmar, and he said: 'Are you not in the state of iḥrām? But—' the hadith..."]]

It is also related from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was asked: "Did you used to dislike trade during the Hajj?" He said: "Was our livelihood anything but trade during the Hajj?" [[al-Ṭabarī narrated it through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muhājir from Abū Ṣāliḥ, the client of ʿUmar, who said: "I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful...' and he mentioned it." In its chain is Mandal ibn ʿAlī, who is weak.]]

Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, recited: ﴿fadlan min rabbikum fī mawāsim al-ḥajj﴾ (a gift from your Lord during the seasons of the Hajj). ﴿in tabtaghū﴾ (in that you seek) ﴿an tabtaghū﴾ [[The words "an tabtaghū" should have been placed before the explanation of His words, ﴿fadlan min rabbikum﴾. (ʿ)]] ﴿afaḍtum﴾: you pressed on in large numbers (dafaʿtum bi-kathrah). It is from the pouring of water, which is pouring abundantly. Its original form was afaḍtum anfusakum (you poured yourselves forth), and the object was omitted, as it is omitted in dafaʿū min mawḍiʿ kadhā (they pushed from such-and-such a place) and ṣabbū (they poured).

In the hadith of Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him [[I have not found it. What is in al-Gharāʾib by Abū ʿUbayd al-Jurmī. In Musnad al-Shāfiʿī and Ṭabaqāt Ibn Saʿd, all from the hadith of Ibn ʿUyaynah from Ibn al-Munkadir, and from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿīd ibn Yarbūʿ from Jubayr ibn al-Ḥuwayrith who said: "I saw Abū Bakr on Qaza', and he was urging his camel with his staff." Al-Jurmī added from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah from Ibn ʿUyaynah: "As if I were looking at his thigh, and it had become uncovered."]]: "He poured forth (ṣabba) at Dafrān, and he was urging (yakhrush) his camel with his staff." [[In some copies it is "Dhafrān," with the letter dhāl and fāʾ. Perhaps the first is with dāl and fāʾ, from al-dafar meaning stench only. Al-dhafar, with dhāl and fāʾ and a vowel, means the sharpness of a smell, whether pleasant or foul, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. As for al-daqar with dāl and qāf, it means harshness, lying, obscenity and slander. This is from al-Ṣiḥāḥ, and in it: al-khirsh is like al-khadsh. (ʿ)]]

They say: "They plunged into the talk (afāḍū fī al-ḥadīth) and burst out with it (ḥaḍabū fīhi)." [[In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: al-haḍbah is a downpour, and haḍaba al-qawm and ihtaḍabū fī al-ḥadīth means they poured into it. (ʿ)]]

﴿ʿArafāt﴾ is a name for the place of standing, named with a plural form like Adhruʿāt. If you say: "Why is it not made diptote (ghayr munṣarif), when it has two causes (of diptotic inflection): the definite form and the feminine?" I say: It cannot be free of the feminine. Either it is with the tāʾ that is in its wording, or with an implied tāʾ, as in Suʿād. The tāʾ in its wording is not a feminine marker. Rather, it is, together with the alif before it, the sign of the feminine plural. The tāʾ cannot be implied in it, because this tāʾ, by being specific to the feminine plural, prevents its being implied, just as the tāʾ of the feminine cannot be implied in bint (daughter), since the tāʾ which replaces the wāw, by being specific to the feminine like the tāʾ of the feminine, refuses to be implied.

They said: It was named so because it was described to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and when he saw it, he recognized it (ʿarafahā). It was said that when Jibrīl was taking him around the holy places, he showed it to him and said: "You have recognized it (qad ʿarafta)." It was said: Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ met there and recognized one another (taʿārafā). It was said: Because people recognize one another there. Allah knows the reality of that best. It is one of the names that were coined (murtajalah), because ʿarafah is not known among the names of kinds, except to be the plural of ʿārif (one who knows).

It was said: In it there is evidence that standing at ʿArafah is obligatory, because the outpouring (ifāḍah) cannot occur except after it. It is related from the Prophet ﷺ: "Hajj is ʿArafah; whoever attains ʿArafah has attained the Hajj." [[Narrated by the compilers of the Sunan and al-Ḥākim, and the wording is from al-Nasāʾī, who added: "before the dawn rises." All of them from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yaʿmar al-Dīlī, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

﴿fa-dhkurū Allāh﴾ (so remember Allah): with the talbiyah, the tahlīl, the takbīr, praise and supplications. It was said: with the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers. ﴿al-mash ʿar al-ḥarām﴾ is Quzaḥ, the mountain on which the Imam stands, and on which there is a fire-beacon (al-mīqadah). It was said: the Mashʿar al-Ḥarām is what lies between the mountain of Muzdalifah, from the two narrow passes of ʿArafah [[His words "from the two narrow passes of ʿArafah": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, al-maʾzam is the narrow passage, and also the place of battle. (ʿ)]] to the valley of Muḥassir. Neither the two passes nor the valley of Muḥassir is part of the Mashʿar al-Ḥarām. The correct view is that it is the mountain, because of what Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, related: that when the Prophet ﷺ prayed the dawn prayer at Muzdalifah in the darkness, he mounted his she-camel and came to the Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, and he supplicated, glorified (kabbara) and declared the unity of Allah (hallala), and he remained standing until it became light. [[Narrated by Muslim in the chapter on the description of the Hajj, in the long hadith.]]

His words ﴿ʿinda al-mash ʿar al-ḥarām﴾ mean: in the direction of the Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, near to it, for the sake of its merit, like being near the Mountain of Mercy. Otherwise, all of Muzdalifah is a place of standing except the valley of Muḥassir. Or the ʿaqāb (rear parts) of Muzdalifah were made to be the Mashʿar, since they have the ruling of the Mashʿar and are joined to it, near the Mashʿar. The mashʿar means the sign, because it is the sign of worship.

It is described as al-ḥarām because of its sanctity. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him, that he looked at the people on the night of Jamʿ and said: "I have seen people this night who do not sleep." It was said: Muzdalifah was called Jamʿ because Ādam, peace be upon him, gathered there with Ḥawwāʾ, and he drew near to her (izdalafa ilayhā), meaning he approached her. It is related from Qatādah: because the two prayers are combined there (yujmaʿu). It is permissible to say: it is described by the act of its people, because they draw near (yazdalifūn) to Allah, that is, they seek nearness by standing there.

﴿kamā hadākum﴾: here mā is either a verbal-source particle (maṣdariyyah) or a preventive particle (kāffah). The meaning: remember Him with a good remembrance, as He guided you with good guidance; and remember Him as He taught you how to remember Him, and do not deviate from it. ﴿wa-in kuntum min qablihi﴾ (though before it you were): before the guidance, ﴿la-mina al-ḍāllīn﴾ (certainly among those who were astray), the ignorant, who did not know how to remember Him and worship Him. Here in is the lightened form of the heavy in (inna), and the lām is the distinguishing lām.

﴿thumma afīḍū﴾ (then pour forth): then let your outpouring be ﴿min ḥaythu afāḍa al-nās﴾ (from where the people poured forth), and do not be from Muzdalifah. This is because of what the Ḥums (Quraysh and their allies) were upon of arrogance over the people and haughtiness over them, and their exalting themselves above standing with the others. And their saying: "We are the people of Allah and the dwellers of His sanctuary, so we will not leave it," and so they stand at Jamʿ while all other people stand at ʿArafāt. [[Maḥmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: "Al-Zamakhsharī, may Allah have mercy on him: 'That is because of what the Ḥums were upon of arrogance over the people...' (etc.)." Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The verse includes two points. First: the coordination of the two outpourings, one upon the other, with a single referent, which is the outpouring commanded. Someone might suppose it is coordination of a thing with itself, and this supposition is removed by the fact that between them there is the difference that exists between the general and the specific: the first statement is the outpouring in its unrestricted form, and the second command is the outpouring restricted by equality with the people. Second: after clarifying the soundness of the coordination, its being introduced by the particle thumma (then), which implies delay in addition to difference, while there is no delay between the absolute and the restricted addition. The answer: delay may be in terms of time, and it may also be in terms of the elevation of rank and the distance in height relative to others, and this is what he answered with after further vigor and clarification.]]

Then you asked: "What is the position of thumma?" I say: Its position is like its position in your saying: "Be kind to people, then do not be kind to other than the noble," where you use thumma to indicate the difference between being kind to the noble and being kind to others, and the distance between them. Likewise, when He commanded them to remember Him at the outpouring from ʿArafāt, He said: "Then pour forth," to show the difference between the two outpourings, and that one of them is correct and the other is mistaken.

It was said: "Then pour forth from where the people poured forth" means the Ḥums, that is, from Muzdalifah to Minā after the outpouring from ʿArafāt. It was read: "min ḥaythu afāḍa al-nāsī" with a kasrah on the sīn, that is, al-nāsī, who is Ādam, from His words: ﴿And We had already made a covenant with Ādam before, but he forgot (fa-nasiya)﴾. It means that the outpouring from ʿArafāt is an ancient law, so do not oppose it.

﴿wa-istaghfirū Allāh﴾ (and ask Allah for forgiveness): for your opposition in the standing place and similar matters of your ignorance. ﴿fa-idhā qaḍaytum manāsikakum﴾ (so when you have completed your rites): that is, when you have finished your acts of worship of Hajj and have departed. ﴿fa-dhkurū Allāh kadhikrikum ābāʾakum﴾ (then remember Allah as you remember your fathers): so increase the remembrance of Allah and go to extremes in it, as you do in remembering your fathers, their glories and their days. When they had completed their rites, they would stand between the mosque at Minā and the mountain, enumerating the virtues of their fathers and mentioning the good qualities of their days.

﴿aw ashadda dhikran﴾ (or with a greater remembrance): in a position of genitive (jarr) by coordination with what the remembrance is attached to in His words ﴿kadhikrikum﴾, as you say: "like the remembrance of Quraysh of their fathers, or of a people greater than them in remembrance." Or in an accusative position by coordination with ābāʾakum, meaning: or more intense in remembrance than your fathers, on the basis that dhikran is the tamyīz (specification) of the one who remembers. ﴿fa-minā al-nās man yaqūlu﴾ (among people is he who says): its meaning is: increase the remembrance and supplication of Allah, for people are divided between one who seeks through the remembrance of Allah nothing but the goods of this world, and one who seeks the good of both abodes. So be among the ones who increase. ﴿rabbanā ātinā fī al-dunyā﴾ (Our Lord, give us in this world): make our giving, that is, our provision, in this world only. ﴿wa-mā lahu fī al-ākhirati min khalāq﴾ (and he has no portion in the Hereafter): that is, whoever seeks my portion (khalāqī), which is share. Or: this caller has no share in the Hereafter, because his concern is limited to this world.

﴿wa-Allāhu sarīʿu al-ḥisāb﴾ (and Allah is swift in reckoning): He is about to establish the Resurrection and call the servants to account. So hasten to increase the remembrance and to seek the Hereafter. Or: He described Himself as swift in reckoning the creatures despite their great number and the abundance of their deeds, to show the perfection of His power and the necessity of being wary of Him.

It is related that He reckons all creation in the time it takes to milk a sheep. It is related: in the time between two milkings of a she-camel. It is related: in the time of a single blink.

فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ ﴿fadlan min rabbikum﴾: an enrichment and a gift from Him, and it means profit and gain through trade.
